products.name: AudioQuest DragonTail Carbon USB A to C Adapter

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Using DragonTail to connect to an external USB DAC, such as an AudioQuest DragonFly, will provide greatly improved audio performance. Solid 5% Silver Conductors Solid conductors eliminate strand-interaction distortion and reduce jitter.

Solid silver-plated conductors are excellent for very high-frequency applications, like HDMI audio and video. These signals, being such a high frequency, travel almost exclusively on the surface of the conductor.

As the surface is made of high-purity silver, the performance is very close to that of a solid silver cable, but priced much closer to solid copper cable. This is an incredibly cost effective way of manufacturing very high-quality HDMI cables.

All Conductors Controlled for RF Noise Directionality Hard-Cell Foam Insulation Hard-Cell Foam (HCF) Insulation ensures critical signal-pair geometry. Any solid material adjacent to a conductor is actually part of an imperfect circuit.

Wire insulation and circuit board materials all absorb energy. Some of this energy is stored and then released as distortion.

Hard-Cell Foam Insulation is similar to the Foamed-PE used in AQ's more affordable Bridges & Falls cables, and is nitrogen-injected to create air pockets. Because nitrogen (like air) does not absorb energy and therefore does not release any energy from or into the conductor, distortion is reduced.

In addition, the stiffness of the material allows the cable's conductors to maintain a stable relationship along the cable's full length, producing a stable impedance character and further minimizing distortion. Carbon-Based Noise- and Crosstalk-Dissipation System This cable's negative conductors are covered with partially conductive Carbon-Loaded Polyethylene.

This remarkable material reduces radio-frequency garbage being fed back into the amplifier. The sonic benefit is exactly the same reduction in "hash" and improved dimensionality that comes whenever RF interference is reduced in an audio circuit.

In addition, a carbon layer damps interaction between positive and negative conductors, and an external Carbon-Based Noise-Dissipation System reduces external interference.

products.name: CrinEar Reference In-Ear Headphones

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The CrinEar Reference is the next step after the CrinEar Daybreak, but it is aimed at a different listener. Where Daybreak earned its following by being balanced, accessible, and easy to recommend, the Reference takes a more exacting approach.

99, it is built around a neutrality-first target for listeners who want tonal accuracy, mix translation, and a more monitor-like presentation from an in-ear. This is not a “Reference” in name only.

CrinEar built it around a deliberately objective tuning target, then refined it so it still sounds believable in practice. The goal is simple: preserve the honesty and linearity you want from a real monitoring tool, while keeping enough physicality in the low end for music to sound complete and lifelike.

CrinEar Reference: We Have Arrived - Written review by Listener CrinEar Reference: Nothing To Prove - Written review by FC-Construct CrinEar Reference vs CrinEar Daybreak The easiest way to understand the Reference is to place it next to the Daybreak. Daybreak was the broader all-rounder, the model that made Crinacle’s tuning philosophy easy to access at a lower price.

The Reference moves upmarket and narrows the mission. It is the more specialized model, tuned for neutrality, consistency, and critical listening rather than broad crowd-pleasing warmth or extra excitement.

That does not make it sterile. It makes it focused.

If Daybreak was designed to be easy to love, the Reference is designed to be easy to trust. For listeners who want an IEM that tells them what is in the recording rather than flattering it, that is the real appeal.

What the Measurements Suggest The B&K 5128 measurements back up that goal. The CrinEar Reference tracks a very even overall slope from bass to treble, with both the short tips and standard tips landing in a range that should read as neutral to neutral-warm for most listeners.

*This shows the CrinEar Reference measurements for each set of tips done on the B&K 5128. These measurements show seatings for each tip size, which change the insertion depth of the IEM and change the sound.

The shaded area shows the outer range of results while the bolded center line shows the more common result, but for any individual, depending on insertion depth, the sound could be anywhere within the shaded area. The bounded field marked by solid lines on top and bottom shows the range of preferences we know to exist from the Harman research, while the dotted center line shows a tilt of 10dB from bass to treble, which aligns with typical listener preferences in both headphones and speakers.

Just as importantly, these measurements show why tip choice matters. Because insertion depth changes the sound, an individual listener may hear something anywhere within that shaded range.

IEMs tend to be sensitive to related to your ears and the Reference is no different. Dialing in the right tip can meaningfully affect how neutral, warm, or direct it sounds in your ears.

Tips matter! Objective Neutrality, Refined for Real Listening CrinEar’s stated target is a population-averaged diffuse-field response with a gentle downward tilt, then a subtle low-frequency lift to restore the sense of physicality people expect from a good speaker system or studio monitor in a real room.

That is an important choice. Plenty of products chase flatness on paper.

Far fewer manage to sound natural once they are actually in your ears. Here, the bass lift is there to preserve realism, not to turn the Reference into a bass-boosted set.

The end result should be familiar to anyone who values accurate monitors: controlled, even-handed, and honest, with enough foundation down low to keep the sound grounded. Tuned for the Studio, Built for Daily Use The Reference is designed as a genuine monitoring tool.

It is meant for critical listening, mix checks, and anyone who wants reliable tonal balance without constantly having to second-guess what the IEM is adding or taking away. Midrange clarity is central to that job.

If vocals, instruments, and the body of the mix are not presented with the right balance and weight, nothing works as a true reference monitor. That is also why the bass system matters so much here.

A flat target is only useful if the low end stays disciplined. The Reference is built to keep bass extension and physicality without letting it blur into the rest of the mix, which makes it more useful for long-term listening and more credible as a tool.

HODWS Architecture and 3BA Driver System Bass is handled by a custom Horizontally-Opposed Dual Woofer System, or HODWS, using two 10 mm dynamic drivers. By splitting the mechanical load across both woofers, the system is designed to reduce stress on each diaphragm, improve bass linearity, improve efficiency, and deliver tighter, more controlled low-end response.

That is a smart way to approach bass on a neutrality-first IEM, because “flat bass” still needs to sound like real bass. For the mids and highs, the Reference uses a three balanced armature array made up of twin Sonion midrange drivers and a Knowles supertweeter.

That gives the Reference a clear division of labor across the frequency range, with the dual dynamic system handling foundation and weight while the BA array focuses on articulation, presence, and upper-end detail. Tip Choice and Fit Matter The included tip selection is not filler.

It is part of how the Reference should be used. Between the standard bore, shorter bore, widebore, and foam options, listeners have multiple ways to tune fit, insertion depth, seal, and final tonal balance.

The measurements show why that matters: seating changes the response, especially as you move through the upper mids and treble. For most people, the Reference should land somewhere between neutral and neutral-warm once properly fitted.

The best approach is to treat the included tips as part of the setup process, not just accessories in the box. The right tip will not only improve comfort and seal, it will help the Reference sound closer to the way it was intended.

Built to Last, Easy to Live With The Reference uses a full aluminum shell precision-machined with a 5-axis CNC process. The pseudo-custom shape is designed to sit securely for longer sessions while helping control enclosure resonance.

It feels purposeful, which suits a product aimed at both serious enthusiasts and professional users. 4 mm balanced connectors.

That makes the Reference easy to move between portable dongles, DAPs, desktop gear, and more serious source chains without needing to swap cables or give up connection flexibility. 4 mm balanced interchangeable connector S/M/L standard bore silicone eartips S/M/L shorter bore silicone eartips XS/S/M/L widebore silicone eartips M foam eartips Leatherette zip case

Note: The Rock Lobster is now back in stock! 4mm cable.

The Clamshell Case is also in stock. THE LEGEND OF THE LOBSTER The history of rock is full of legendary frontpeople: from Freddie Mercury, who could command a stadium with his voice, to Ozzy Osbourne, who could level a hotel room under the influence of whatever he was on at the time.

Henry Rollins, Jimi Hendrix, Karen O: artists who embody freedom, fearlessness, and a really good time. These were our inspirations for the Rock Lobster.

We set out to create an IEM you could take anywhere, plug into virtually anything, and count on to hold its own in any corner of the rock genre. Something you’d always want with you, whether you’re connecting it to a phone, a portable player, or a desktop DAC/amp.

We wanted an IEM that could do justice to the rumbling power of a John Bonham drum fill without drowning out the delicate croon of Robert Plant. One that could shimmer like the chimes at the start of a Cure song without wearing you down with sibilance.

A pan-genre, everyday-carry IEM for lovers of rock music. Where Is My Mid?

When most people think “rock headphone,” they think big, pounding bass and sparkly treble, but the unsung hero of a great rock IEM is the mids. You need enough separation to pick apart the guitars, singers, backup singers, synths, and everything else crashing together in the mix.

The Rock Lobster delivers just that: natural mids with clarity and space, and deep-digging bass and sparkling treble. Baby Driver With a low impedance of 32Ω, the Rock Lobster is easy to drive.

Plug it into your phone, iPod, or laptop and you’re good to go. ” Give it the proper gear and it really comes alive.

We’ve been loving it on everything from a trusty old 5th gen iPod to a FiiO DAP to the Gremlin/Merlin stack—and it scales beautifully with all of them. (Keep it silicone, stupid) ear tips We went through dozens of ear tips to find the right ones, testing everything from silicone to memory foam.

Some muddied the mids, some choked the bass, some did unspeakable horrors to the treble. In the end, we landed on a simple pair of silicone tips that brings a satisfying and enveloping low-end kick without smothering the separation in the mids.

Sometimes simpler is better. Walk the line: A Cable that doesn’t go overboard Tuning a rock IEM is tricky, and the cable is a big part of that equation.

Some rock, like punk and garage, actually suffers from too much clarity and detail: all those imperfections get laid bare like when the houselights come up during the middle of a set. On the other hand, a bad cable just muddies everything, which kills the separation and texture you need for bands like TOOL or Radiohead.

After testing everything from bargain bin wires to boutique cables that cost more than the IEMs themselves, we landed on a cable that strikes the right balance: enough clarity to reveal the details, but not so pristine that it robs the Ramones of their gritty charm. 4mm.

I’ve Just Seen a Faceplate Like the best frontpeople, the Rock Lobster knows how to strike a balance: understated when it needs to be, electric when the spotlight hits. The black “lobster tail” faceplate is cool and muted, easy to wear on the subway or in the office without attracting attention.

The 109 PRO uses a combination of walnut wood, zinc, manganese steel, and vegan leather in a comfortable, lightweight, yet highly durable structure. Velour ear pads Velour cushions comfortably surround the ears, providing the optimal seal for creating natural sound.

products.name: Matrix Audio MS-1 Flagship Music Streamer

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Note: This product is currently sold out. If you're interested in purchasing it, please contact customer support.

Perfect Creation The all-new M series marks a milestone for Matrix Audio as it advances toward traditional Hi-Fi systems. The lineup includes the MS-1 music streamer, MP-1 preamplifier, and MA-1 power amplifier—together forming a complete flagship system that reflects Matrix Audio’s understanding of high-fidelity sound.

The M series is the first to adopt the new Matrix Design language, setting the direction for the future evolution of Matrix Audio products. Matrix Design Evaluating audio products from the dimensions of listening and looking has always been central to our philosophy.

From concept to execution, every step reflects a love for music and a pursuit of beauty. The MS-1 embodies simplicity in its industrial design.

Hundreds of circular perforations of varying sizes and depths are arranged across its hexahedral surface, creating a rhythmic visual pattern reminiscent of musical beats emerging across the chassis. Focus On Software Experience The source device is the soul of an audio system.

Hardware forms the body of the MS-1, while software shapes its character. Beyond sound quality, we emphasize usability—simplifying interaction and highlighting music information on the display.

Through the MA Remote App, you can control your entire system from your listening position. Volume adjustments, track selection, playback control, filter settings, operating modes, and display brightness are all managed seamlessly from your phone or tablet, powered by the carefully developed MA Player system.

MA Player MA Player is a streamlined Linux-based software system designed specifically for Hi-Fi playback and exclusively available on Matrix Audio products. It has evolved to deliver enhanced playback performance, expanded functionality, and a refined interactive experience tailored to high-resolution audio systems.

MA Remote App The MA Remote App serves as the core control center for Matrix Audio music streamers. Installed on iPhone, iPad, or Android devices, it allows you to browse and play local music libraries and stream high-resolution content from services such as SONY Select, TIDAL, Qobuz, HIGHRESAUDIO, Baidu Cloud, and QQ Music, as well as online radio.

Even when streaming through Roon or other applications, track information can still be viewed through MA Remote. The app also enables full configuration of hardware settings.

PCM Resampling & DSD Conversion The built-in asynchronous upsampling and DSD conversion engine processes audio entirely within the digital domain. Asynchronous resampling and interpolation help isolate jitter and enhance detail retrieval.

The DSD conversion engine can transform playback into DSD format, increasing perceived density and refinement. Adjustable PCM and DSD conversion parameters allow for tailored sonic preferences.

IIS-LVDS Digital Output The MS-1 functions as a high-performance audio transport, outputting all playback signals—including analog and phono inputs—through its IIS-LVDS port. This enables connection to external DACs for expanded system flexibility and varied listening configurations.

Analog Input & Phono Input Two pairs of line inputs and one phono input are provided. Balanced XLR and single-ended RCA inputs integrate external analog sources, while the built-in phono stage supports both MM and MC cartridges for direct turntable connection.

All analog signals are digitized via a high-precision ADC, processed internally, and can be routed to the IIS-LVDS output. Digital Audio Input Comprehensive digital inputs—including USB, optical, coaxial, and IIS-LVDS—allow the MS-1 to operate as a high-end DAC.

Computers, CD transports, set-top boxes, and gaming consoles can connect directly, enabling high-quality digital-to-analog conversion through the MS-1’s internal architecture. Preamplifier & Dual Balanced Output The MS-1 Pre includes a built-in preamplifier with precision resistor array volume control.

The multi-stage op-amp design provides +10dB gain and up to 16VRMS output, allowing direct connection to power amplifiers or active speakers. A fixed-level XLR output is also available for simultaneous recording or monitoring applications.

Dual D/A Chip Independent Channel Design The MS-1 is Matrix Audio’s first platform built around dual AK4191 and AK4499 flagship DAC chipsets. Each operates in mono mode with independent left and right channel PCB assemblies, forming a true dual-mono design.

This configuration delivers precise signal reproduction and extended dynamic range. Precision Resistor Volume Control The integrated resistor ladder volume control uses four control units composed of 64 precision resistors with 1‰ accuracy and 32 sealed reed relays controlled by an MCU.

This voltage-divider architecture ensures consistent channel matching, minimal signal degradation, and near-silent operation during adjustment. DPLL High Precision Clock A high-performance DPLL clock synthesis circuit generates an ultra-low jitter signal, reaching as low as 45 femtoseconds.

The MS-1 also supports connection to an external 10MHz reference clock, allowing further refinement of digital timing accuracy. Expandable SFP Fiber Optic Network Port An SFP interface enables fiber optic network connectivity, isolating electrical interference from upstream network equipment.

This optical isolation enhances system purity while maintaining a standard Ethernet port for traditional network integration. NVMe SSD Slot An internal NVMe SSD slot on the underside of the chassis allows installation of high-speed solid-state storage.

This design eliminates reliance on external drives and avoids vibration or noise associated with traditional HDDs. Stored music can be managed via network sharing or transferred using the MA Remote App.

Square Copper Wire Transformer & Linear Power Two custom toroidal transformers with square copper windings separately power the digital and analog sections. Square copper conductors increase surface area and current capacity while lowering resistance, improving transient response.

MUNDORF M-Lytic AG capacitors and multiple low-noise LDO regulators ensure stable, clean power delivery throughout the system. H-Shaped Chassis Structure The H-shaped structural design is built around a 20mm CNC-machined aluminum main beam that supports the entire chassis.

Components mount directly to this core structure, creating isolated internal cavities that reduce interference between modules. Symmetrical channel layout enhances both structural integrity and visual balance.

Elegant Industrial Design & Refined Build Quality The refined industrial design reflects the Matrix Design language through precise CNC machining and carefully finished surfaces. Each component features a matte texture that conveys craftsmanship, delivering a cohesive and understated visual presence.

Pure & Clear The MS-1 delivers a balanced and natural presentation that remains faithful to the recording. Every detail of the M series reflects careful development, calibration, and refinement by the Matrix Audio team, uniting design, engineering, and craftsmanship into a coherent flagship system.

A new baseline for balanced sound The K7 has a six-stage audio circuit with truly balanced analog and digital sections, which helps to reduce crosstalk and reproduce music faithfully and noiselessly. Balanced amplification couldn’t sound better Using the same THX AAA 788+ amplifiers as the K9 Pro, the K7 is capable of outputting 560mW into a 300Ω load at 1% distortion, and 200mW into a 32Ω load at 1% distortion.

This ensures both low and high impedance headphones are fully powered with optimal musicality. Dual AK4493SEQ D/A chips The left and right channels are each equipped with an efficient high-performance AK4493SEQ D/A chip.

Worry-free listening Overheating, overload, and DC protection systems ensure that the K7 always operates at its best, so you can always enjoy a worry-free listening experience. Multiple independent power stages The K7 features a power design consisting of multiple independent stages, with the voltage of each stage regulated by low-noise LDOs.

Feeding this power design is an external 12V switching power supply. All in all, the K7’s power design supplies plentiful, clean power for an extraordinary listening experience.

Smooth operator The K7 features an all-aluminum alloy construction, carefully finished with CNC and other processes. Its elegant black color is perfectly complemented by the gold accents of the THX and Hi-Res Audio badges and the splashes of color from the RGB lights.

overviewFields.title: Description

True R2R sound for under $200 Experience a new dimension of audio fidelity with the FiiO K11 R2R Balanced Desktop DAC/Amp. Designed for audiophiles who crave authentic sound, this DAC/Amp is packed with advanced features that bring your music to life.

From its fully differential true 24bit R2R DAC to its customizable RGB lighting, the K11 R2R offers a totally immersive listening experience. Fully differential true 24-bit R2R DAC resistor arrays The K11 R2R features FIIO's self-developed four-channel fully differential 24bit R2R DAC.

1% tolerance and low temperature drift (30ppm). This meticulous configuration delivers a unique and charming sound, capturing every nuance of your favorite tracks.

Dual NOS/OS modes NOS (Non-Oversampling) Mode: Preserves the original sampling rate for decoding—maintaining the authentic sound of your music. OS (Oversampling) Mode: Upsamples to a high sampling rate of 384kHz, providing superior audio performance with even more refined, clear sound.

True 24-bit decoding Supporting PCM 384kHz/24bit and DSD256 decoding, the K11 R2R can easily handle high-precision audio signals. *DSD256 requires setting the DSD output mode to Native on the source device, internally converting to PCM before being decoded by the R2R resistor arrays.

NJW1195A high-quality electronic volume control The K11 R2R uses the NJW1195A, a 4-channel electronic volume controller. 3 gain levels + 3 independent volume curves With three independent gain levels and volume curves, the K11 R2R adapts to various types of headphones, whether you're using sensitive earphones or harder-to-drive over-ear headphones.

This customization ensures a tailored listening experience. Digital audio bridge: specially-designed audio circuit The K11 R2R employs a sophisticated audio circuit.

The audio signal is transmitted via a USB interface processor to a digital audio bridge, then processed by an FPGA before being sent to the R2R DAC for 4-channel output. It passes through two Ti OPA1642 op-amps for low-pass filtering and single-ended analog signal converting, then to the NJW1195A for precise volume adjustment.

Finally, two SGM8262 op-amps handle 4-way phase inversion and amplification, resulting in balanced and single-ended analog outputs. Specially-designed power supply The K11 R2R's power supply system uses up to 17 low-noise LDO precision regulator ICs and two DC-DC converters, providing multi-channel specialized power supplies.

Combined with an external custom 12V switching power supply, it ensures the purity of the power and supports strong power output. This results in a stable, clean power supply and high-quality sound.

1300mW + 1300mW Powerful output With the capability to push 1300mW+1300mW under balanced modes, the K11 R2R can drive many HiFi earphones and headphones, unlocking their full potential and delivering powerful, detailed audio. High-contrast LCD screen A custom, high-contrast LCD screen allows you to easily see the sampling rate, volume, gain, or output mode at a glance.

The durable screen is always on with no burn-in, ensuring you always have the information you need with none of the drawbacks of lesser screens. One source of total control The K11 R2R's multi-function volume knob controls power, menu operations, volume adjustments, and other functions.

Quickly switch between PO/PRE (LO SE)/LO modes by double-pressing the knob. Adjustable RGB logo lighting The FIIO logo features RGB lighting, helping you quickly identify the sampling rate of the current audio.

Six LED strips and reflective design elements ensure uniform and elegant lighting. Comprehensive safety systems RCA metal pressing: Enhanced stability, reliable connection, and durability.

Headphone amplifier heat dissipation upgrade: Thermal silicone gel and aluminum alloy ensure fast heat dissipation. Exclusive phosphor copper metal shielding: Provides corrosion resistance and anti-oxidation capabilities, effectively resisting external interference for accurate signal processing.

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
A new way to hear your music The K13 R2R is a fully-balanced desktop DAC and headphone amplifier that leans on FIIO’s proprietary 24-bit R2R resistor arrays, a powerful 2400mW+2400mW balanced output, and a wealth of tuning and connectivity options. With dual NOS/OS modes, LDAC Bluetooth, and a precision 10-band PEQ, it gives you control over both the flavor and fidelity of your music.

Fully differential 24-bit R2R DAC At the heart of the K13 R2R are four channels of resistor arrays: 48 precision-thin film resistors per channel, 192 in total. 1% accuracy with ultra-low temperature drift.

The result is a true 24-bit fully differential R2R DAC that delivers a sound signature that’s rich, organic, and natural. Lower FFT harmonics mean darker backgrounds and less noise, so what you hear is only the music.

Double the fun with Dual NOS/OS modes NOS (Non-Oversampling) Mode: Maintains the original sampling rate for decoding, preserving the authentic sound and allowing you to enjoy an organic and captivating musical experience. OS (Oversampling) Mode: Upsamples globally to a high sampling rate of 384kHz, for superior audio performance and even more refined, clear sound.

Preamplifier + power amplifier output With a wide variety of inputs and outputs, this unit functions as both a preamplifier and a power amplifier, catering to various listening preferences. 10-band high-precision PEQ Fine-tune the sound to your taste.

The built-in parametric EQ, powered by the XMOS XU316 chip and FIIO’s proprietary tuning algorithm, supports 10-band adjustment across all modes. Use the FIIO Control app or web interface to load presets like “Retro PEQ,” match headphone response curves, or share your own EQ curves.

Balanced from start to finish From DAC to LPF to volume control and headphone amp, the entire circuit is fully differential. That means minimal distortion, excellent interference rejection, and a dynamic range that stays intact across the chain.

Add gain control, headphone protection, and POP noise elimination, and you get a circuit that’s as safe as it is clean. Specially-designed power supply DC/AC dual supplies: The 30W internal supply is shielded for reduced interference, while an external DC input lets you experiment with higher-end linear supplies.

Multi-rail design: 18 low-noise LDOs and 5 DC-DC converters keep each section fed with clean power. Audiophile-grade capacitors: ELNA RA3 silk-film electrolytics and specialized tantalum caps help deliver warmth and stability.

Power on tap With 2400mW+2400mW into 32Ω on the balanced outputs, the K13 R2R has the muscle to drive high-impedance headphones with ease while still being gentle enough for sensitive IEMs. 3 gain levels + 3 independent volume curves The 3 independent gain levels and volume curves allow the K13 R2R to give you a better listening experience with various types of headphones, whether you are using sensitive earphones or harder to drive over-ear headphones.

Analog and digital - separate power supplies for cleaner audio By keeping the power supplies for the digital and analog circuits separate, the K17 reduces interference and crosstalk, giving you purer audio signal, free from unwanted noise or distortion.

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Fully-balanced headphone amplifier The VMV P2 MKII is a fully-balanced desktop headphone amplifier and preamplifier engineered for demanding headphones, sensitive IEMs, and high-performance two-channel systems. Its 99-piece parallel op-amp architecture, ultra-low distortion PLFC+ circuit, and integrated GaN power supply deliver exceptional current capability, low output impedance, and remarkable signal purity.

99-piece parallel amplification architecture The P2 MKII utilizes 99 low-noise operational amplifiers in a parallel configuration to improve current delivery and reduce output impedance. This design allows the amplifier to maintain authority with both high-impedance headphones and current-hungry planar magnetic designs while preserving low-noise performance for sensitive in-ear monitors.

Balanced output reaches up to 14W per channel at 16Ω and 8W per channel at 32Ω. Fully-balanced PLFC+ circuit design A true differential signal path extends from input to output, minimizing common-mode noise and maintaining channel separation throughout the amplification stage.

00006% with a signal-to-noise ratio up to 135dB. Integrated GaN power supply The built-in Gallium Nitride switching power supply combines high efficiency with low-noise operation.

Compared to traditional switching designs, the GaN implementation reduces switching losses and ripple interference while supplying substantial current reserves during dynamic passages. This contributes to a quieter background and improved control across a wide range of headphones.

Three gain levels for headphones and IEMs The P2 MKII includes selectable Low, Mid, and High gain modes for improved compatibility with different headphones and earphones. Low gain is specifically optimized for high-sensitivity IEMs, helping reduce hiss and improve usable volume range.

A custom high-precision volume potentiometer further minimizes channel imbalance at low listening levels. Desktop preamplifier functionality In addition to headphone amplification, the P2 MKII operates as a dedicated preamplifier with both RCA and XLR pre-outs.

This allows direct connection to power amplifiers or active speakers for integration into a compact desktop or full-size stereo system. Internally, the amplifier uses low-temperature-drift resistors to maintain consistent performance over long listening sessions and changing operating temperatures.

Protection systems and firmware support Built-in DC, overload, over-voltage, and thermal protection circuits help safeguard connected headphones and the amplifier itself. A delayed startup relay design suppresses power-on transients for pop-free operation.

The rear USB service port supports future firmware updates and system optimization. 25kg) What’s included VMV P2 MKII headphone amplifier AC power cable User manual

overviewFields.title: Description

Cayin N3Ultra digital audio player The Cayin N3Ultra is a portable digital audio player built around dual AKM DACs, a Gen3 vacuum tube audio circuit, and a fully-customized Android-based system focused on local playback. It combines solid-state and tube timbres, balanced and single-ended outputs, and practical power for everyday listening at home or on the move.

Designed to work equally well as a standalone player, USB DAC, or digital transport, N3Ultra fits naturally into a listening routine that moves between headphones, IEMs, and external amplifiers. Dual AKM DAC architecture The N3Ultra uses two AK4493S DAC chips operating in mono mode, dedicating one DAC to each channel.

This fully differential design reduces crosstalk and improves channel separation, helping preserve spatial cues and low-level detail. Independent analog circuits for left and right channels support cleaner signal handling from conversion through output.

Selectable tube and solid-state timbres A Gen3 vacuum tube audio circuit built around Raytheon JAN6418 NOS tubes allows you to choose between Classic tube, Modern tube, and solid-state timbres. Each mode adjusts circuit behavior rather than applying digital coloration, letting you tailor tonal character based on headphones, music library, or listening environment.

4mm balanced headphone outputs, each supporting tube and solid-state operation. Balanced output delivers up to 600mW at 32Ω, providing enough headroom for demanding portable headphones while remaining quiet with sensitive IEMs.

Precision volume control Volume adjustment is handled by a JRC NJW1195A four-channel electronic volume controller, a design commonly used in preamplifiers. This approach maintains channel balance at low listening levels and reduces noise compared to conventional digital attenuation.

Low-jitter clocking and signal control Two Accusilicon AS318 femtosecond oscillators provide clock signals with very low phase noise, supporting accurate timing during digital-to-analog conversion. An FPGA manages re-clocking, de-jittering, and signal reshaping, helping maintain consistency across PCM and DSD playback.

1 system powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon 425 processor. System-level sample rate conversion is bypassed using Cayin’s DTA implementation, allowing audio files to reach the DAC without unwanted processing.

The included Cayin Music app focuses on local playback rather than background services. 1-inch color touchscreen with a 720 × 1280 resolution provides clear navigation and album art display.

Physical buttons and a volume knob remain available for one-handed use. The illuminated home button doubles as a sampling rate indicator, offering quick visual confirmation of playback format.

Flexible connectivity The N3Ultra functions as a USB DAC, USB digital transport, or standalone player. USB-C supports audio input and output, OTG storage, and S/PDIF coaxial output through a USB-embedded connection.

overviewFields.title: Solid Perfect-Surface Copper (PSC) Conductors
overviewFields.value: Perfect-Surface Copper has an astonishingly smooth and pure surface. Proprietary metal-processing technology protects the wire’s surface at every stage of drawing and fabrication. When high-purity low-oxide copper is kept as soft, pure, and smooth as possible, it becomes a wonderfully low-distortion conductor. For over 30 years AudioQuest has pioneered the use of superior metals; yet most people were surprised by this huge leap in performance. PSC clearly outperforms previous AQ metals that cost over ten times as much. Electrical and magnetic interaction between strands in a conventional cable is the greatest source of distortion, often causing a somewhat dirty, harsh sound. Solid conductors are fundamental toward achieving Red River’s very clean sound.

overviewFields.title: Nitrogen-Injected Hard-Cell Foam Insulation
overviewFields.value: Nitrogen-Injected Hard-Cell Foam insulation is used exclusively in most of AudioQuest’s video and digital audio cables. Similar to Foamed-PE, it is nitrogen-injected to create air pockets. ‘Hard’ foam is used because the stiffness of the material allows the conductors in the cable to maintain the same relationship with each other along the full length of the cable, thus ensuring that the characteristic impedance of the cable is consistent.

overviewFields.title: Metal-Layer Noise-Dissipation System (NDS)

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Old Ways Are Calling Built around a fully-discrete R2R ladder, the Druid converts digital data into analog waveforms through a precise network of resistors rather than a high-speed modulation process. Each resistor contributes a tiny part of the signal, forming a sound that feels natural, human, and grounded in something older than silicon.

This DAC does not compute. It communes.

The first R2R DAC with swappable op-amps The idea came straight from the community: give the upcoming R2R DAC swappable op-amps. What started as a suggestion turned into one of our favorite parts of the Druid.

The open-chassis design made perfect sense for it: no case to crack open, no hidden screws, just clear access to the sockets. We’re glad the community pushed us on this one, because it made the Druid into an even more satisfying product.

Need help swapping op-amps? Op-Amp Restrictions If you're planning to roll op-amps, please note the current draw restrictions.

Given the Druid's compact design, no single op-amp may draw more than 10mA. Exceeding this risks overheating, unwanted noise, or potential damage to the unit.

Always be sure to check the DC characteristics of the op-amp you intend to use before installing it in the Druid. Any single op-amp that requires more than 10mA of current will not perform properly.

5mm. When it came to choosing the stock op-amps, we didn't start with any particular sound or spec sheet advantage in mind—just a price point and the goal of being wowed.

We tested everything we could get our hands on, and the Texas Instruments LM4562NA/NOPB stood out immediately. It handled the midrange with an easy, natural smoothness that made vocals and acoustic instruments feel alive.

Especially paired with the Gremlin, it brought a smile to our faces. XLR balanced outputs For those running balanced chains, the Druid provides a 4V XLR output that delivers all the current and control you’d expect from a fully differential stage.

5mm line out instead of dual RCA jacks. 5mm-to-RCA adapter is included in the box, letting you run the Druid into any single-ended amplifier or powered speaker chain.

XMOS XU316 USB interface At the heart of the Druid’s digital stage is the XMOS XU316, one of the most capable USB controller chips available today. It handles data transfer with rock-solid stability and ultra-low latency, ensuring every bit arrives exactly as intended.

With sixteen cores running in parallel, it keeps high-resolution audio streams (PCM 768kHz, DSD256) moving effortlessly, without adding timing errors or background noise. STACK THE PARTY Add the Stacker to your order if you plan on using the Druid R2R with the Gremlin amp.

This translucent acrylic platform lets you stack the two together like a proper adventuring party. It's precision-cut to cradle the Gremlin's lower acrylic plate and keep it snugly perched without adhesive or screws.

Our very own Sean Flynn designed the stacker, and our buddies at Salad made it a reality. We’ve priced it to be a no-profit product—the price you pay simply covers our costs.

But we’d like to keep the DIY community ethos going, so we’re working with Salad to make it an open-source download on GitHub. Print it, tweak it, remix.

Sound unbound Designed and built in Houston, Texas, the Horizon Closed Carbon Headphones deliver a non-fatiguing, holographic sound with exceptional imaging and precise details. Made for audiophiles, music producers, and gamers needing image-perfect audio cues, the Horizon Closed Carbon combines the natural feel of open-back headphones with the noise isolation of a closed-back design.

Hand-made planar magnetic drivers Jeffrey Yin of SJY Audio hand-builds each driver with the strongest-grade magnets and a full aluminum frame, minimally dampening the driver to guarantee a playful, engaging, and image-perfect sound experience. This setup delivers outstanding performance with crystal clear vocals and a balanced sound across the frequency range.

Carbon fiber ear cups Hand-casted from forged carbon fiber, the ear cups sport a unique “brushstroke” pattern and extreme durability. The matte finish—both scratch- and finger-print resistant—perfectly complements the subtle and strong CNC-machined aluminum frame.

All-day lightweight wearability Built with CNC aluminum construction yet weighing just a pound, the Horizon Closed Carbon offers a sturdy yet lightweight design. Ultra-comfortable ear pads The earpads feature an interior of memory foam that contours to your head.

The outer layer combines perforated protein leather on the inside and non-perforated protein leather on the outside, while the front is made from breathable polyester to reduce heat for a cool and comfortable experience even during all-day use. Full-grain leather headband The top strap is crafted from full-grain leather, chosen for its natural texture and softness, while the bottom strap features thicker full-grain leather with a heavier finish, for its wear resistance.

Together, they form a two-layer construction, boasting long-lasting durability and a classic, refined aesthetic. How we’re listening to it Tom at Apos here.

I first heard the Horizon Closed at CanJam SoCal 2024. I was an immediate fan, loving it for its incredible detail, laser-precise imaging, and delightfully engaging tonality.

I’ve become an even bigger fan since getting to know Jeffrey Yin of SJY and getting a pair of my own to try with my setup at home, where I’ve listened to it for dozens of hours on end. Truly, it’s my favorite headphone I’ve heard in a long time.

While the Horizon Closed sounds great on almost any setup, it really shines with dedicated DAC/amp systems. It's sensitive enough to work with my iPhone 16 Pro and the Moondrop Dawn Pro dongle DAC (though I have to max out the volume).

It also sounds great on hybrid tube amps like the Gremlin, but I much prefer it with solid state amps. Some of my favorite pairings are the FiiO M17, TOPPING D90 stack, xDuoo XA-02 Class-A DAC/Amp, and R2R DACs like the FiiO K11 R2R or Denafrips Ares II.

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Hi Fi, Low Impedance Following the success of the LCD-2 and LCD-3 headphones, Audeze set out to develop a planar magnetic that uses a thinner and lighter transducer. The result is the LCD-X, a headphone thats so smooth, so responsive, and so extended in its frequency response that they made Zeos Reviews proclaim: "everything is garbage compared to these.

" The overall tonality of the LCD-X is neutral, making it a great option for producers and mastering engineers. However, it's so easy to drive that it would make a great pair for everyday listening.

Like other high-end planar magnetics, the LCD-X has a snappiness and punchiness, as well as tight, well-controlled bass. Lifelike reproduction Planar magnetic transducers are different from the dynamic drivers found in most headphones.

A large, thin diaphragm is suspended between two sizable magnets. The magnets create a magnetic field that vibrates the diaphragm to generate sound.

This results in low distortion and incredibly lifelike sound. Fazor Phase Management While planar magnetic headphones offer a lot of advantages over dynamic drivers, they also present their own problems.

Diffraction of sound off the magnets can cause different frequencies to arrive at different times, resulting in changes of phase. And when sound waves created by multiple magnets collide, wave interference occurs (that's a bad thing).

Audeze has attempted to solve these problems with a proprietary technology called Fazor Phase Management. Fazors are triangular elements that cap each magnet.

They act as guides for the sound, maneuvering waves from the drivers and preventing them from interfering with each other. The result is cleaner sound, greater resolution, and better imaging.

Handcrafted comfort Fully assembled in Audeze's Orange County factory, the LCD-X bears the fruit of hand-crafted attention in every stitch. The perforated leather headband and yoked ear cups accommodate a wide variety of head shapes and sizes.

The memory foam ear pads are thick and deep for maximum comfort. " -The Honest Audiophile

Instead of a single attachment on the outer circumference of the transducer, both outer and inner edges of the “ring” are secured to the drive unit. The voice coil excites the diaphragm, connected to the v-shaped groove found near the center of the ring.

products.name: TOPPING A90 Discrete Headphone Amp

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Our best-selling amplifier “Mr. ” These are a few of nicknames the TOPPING A90, our best-selling amplifier, has gained since its release.

At its most basic level, it’s a balanced amp and pre-amp with tremendously clean and powerful output. At its broadest level, it’s become the benchmark by which all other solid state amplifiers below $1,000 are judged.

D for Discrete The A90 Discrete, or A90D, is an upgraded version of the groundbreaking A90. As its name suggests, the A90D uses fully discrete components in a complete redesign of the A90 NFCA module.

Four discrete NFCA modules using 39 transistors each form the fully balanced amp architecture. The matched precision transistors ensure unparalleled distortion and noise performance.

Calling all cans Planar magnetic, dynamic drivers, IEMs—pick your poison, the A90D can handle it. Thanks to its high output voltage, high output current, and low output impedance, the A90D can push loads of power into high-impedance full-sized headphones or pare that power back in order to drive sensitive IEMs.

And with an ultra-low noise rating and high dynamic range, the A90D does it all without producing any audible noise. Say goodbye to ground loop noise When multiple pieces of equipment are used in conjunction, ground loop noise can occur.

Ground loop noise most often manifests as a buzzing or humming sound, which is capable of being loud enough to damage speakers. Although it's known to happen most often in single-ended feeds, it can happen in balanced feeds, too.

The A90D solves this issue with a GND/LIFT switch. When in normal use, set the switch to GND.

If you encounter ground loop noise, set the switch to LIFT, which will change the ground point of the A90D from its chassis to the equipment it’s connected to, eliminating the noise. Pre-amp mode With the A90D in pre-amp mode, connect a power amplifier to drive bookshelf, desktop, or floor speakers.

You can also connect the A90D to the D90SE/LE DAC in pre-amp mode to create a complete high-end sound system. 12V trigger Wouldn’t it be nice if every time you turned on the A90D, the TOPPING LA90 came on automatically, or vice versa?

That’s possible thanks to the A90D’s 12V trigger interface. Set it to active (trigger out) or passive (trigger in), and it can be turned on and off synchronously with other devices equipped with a 12V trigger interface.

R2R volume control The A90D uses an R2R volume control composed of relays and resistor networks, bringing the advantages of precise control, longevity, and complete channel balance. Volume memorization Set the A90D to memorize the output volume settings of the pre-amp, headphone amp, and PRE+HPA modes, and automatically restore to the last volume used when the same output is selected in the future.

WALK THE LINE: A CABLE THAT DOESN’T GO OVERBOARD Tuning a rock IEM is tricky, and the cable is a big part of that equation. Every March 17 on St. Patrick’s Day, New York City merely paints a green line down the center of its Fifth Avenue parade route—a stunt easily pulled off by any city—but only Chicago dyes an entire river the perfect shade of emerald green to honor Irish culture.

Why green? Thanks to Ireland’s lush vegetation, the island is often lovingly referred to as the Emerald Isle.

To the Irish, a green display of pride is not to be taken lightly. In the United States, even those of non-Irish descent know to wear green clothing on St.

Patrick’s Day, or else be playfully pinched by an Irish friend or colleague! But it’s one thing to don a green shirt or tie, another thing altogether to transform a 156-mile long river.

Chicago’s Stephen M. Bailey, the man who orchestrated the transformation, boasted that he’d turn the River Chicago into the River Shannon (Ireland’s longest) for a day, and, eventually, he did.

There was no specific recipe for successfully dyeing a river. A bit of trial and error was required.

Initially, over 100 pounds of dye was used, and the river stayed green for a week! In the second year, 50 pounds of dye kept the river green for three full days.

In the third year, it was found that using 25 pounds of dye would turn the river green for a single day. Two years later, environmental concerns led to the formation of a new vegetable-based dye that produces a perfect sea of green and lasts for four or five hours—40 pounds of the stuff does the trick.

Following suit across the nation, major canals, minor creeks, city blocks, drinking fountains, and even the Presidential Fountain at the White House are dyed green for St. Patrick’s Day—all thanks to the wonderful example set in Chicago.

SOLID LONG-GRAIN COPPER (LGC) CONDUCTORS: Solid conductors eliminate strand-interaction distortion. Chicago’s solid Long-Grain Copper allows a smoother and clearer sound than cables using regular OFHC (Oxygen-Free High-Conductivity) copper.

OFHC is a general metal industry specification regarding “loss” without any concern for distortion. LGC has fewer oxides within the conducting material, less impurities, less grain boundaries, and definitively better performance.

NITROGEN-INJECTED HARD-CELL FOAM INSULATION: Nitrogen-Injected Hard-Cell Foam insulation is used exclusively in most of AudioQuest’s video and digital audio cables. ‘Hard’ foam is used because the stiffness of the material allows the conductors in the cable to maintain the same relationship with each other along the full length of the cable, thus ensuring that the characteristic impedance of the cable is consistent.

METAL-LAYER NOISE-DISSIPATION SYSTEM (NDS): 100% shield coverage is easy. Preventing captured RF Interference from modulating the equipment’s ground reference requires AQ’s Noise-Dissipation System.

Noise-Dissipation System prevents a significant amount of RFI from reaching the equipment’s ground plane. DOUBLE-BALANCED GEOMETRY: Two ideal audio conductors separate from the cable’s shield.

Not only does this prevent the shield from being used as an inferior audio path, but it further optimizes sound quality by only grounding the shield at one end, reducing system ground-plane modulation. COLD-WELDED GOLD-PLATED PLUGS: This plug design allows for a connection devoid of solder, which is a common source of distortion.

Because the ground shells are stamped instead of machined, the metal can be chosen for low distortion instead of machinability.

Connect amplifiers, receivers, soundbars, and AVRs to a broad range of subwoofers with this AudioQuest Greyhound RCA subwoofer cable. 5% Silver conductors minimize distortion, Foamed-Polyethylene preserves dynamic contrasts, and a Metal-Layer Noise-Dissipation efficiently dissipates high-frequency noise.

The result is clearer, naturally beautiful music, intelligible dialog, and thrilling sound effects. 5% Silver Conductors Solid conductors eliminate strand-interaction distortion.

Solid silver-plated conductors are excellent for very high-frequency applications. These signals, being such a high frequency, travel almost exclusively on the surface of the conductor.

As the surface is made of high-purity silver, the performance is very close to that of a solid silver cable, but priced much closer to solid copper cable. This is an incredibly cost effective way of manufacturing very high-quality subwoofer cables.

Metal-Layer Noise-Dissipation It's easy to accomplish 100% shield coverage. Preventing captured radio-frequency interference (RFI) from modulating the equipment's ground reference requires AQ's Noise-Dissipation.

Traditional shield systems typically absorb and then drain noise/RF energy to component ground, modulating and distorting the critical "reference" ground plane, which in turn causes a distortion of the signal. Noise-Dissipation "shields the shield," absorbing and reflecting most of this noise/RF energy before it reaches the layer attached to ground.

Foamed-Polyethylene Insulation Any solid material adjacent to a conductor is actually part of an imperfect circuit. Wire insulation and circuit board materials all absorb energy.

Some of this energy is stored and then released as distortion. Because air absorbs next to no energy and Polyethylene is low-loss and has a benign distortion profile, Foamed-PE, with its high air content, causes much less of the out-of-focus effect common to other materials.

Hyperlitz Coax Geometry A perfect circle of eight negative conductors spiral around a single, larger positive conductor, creating a cable with a large cross-sectional area, minimizing the drawbacks of skin effect, and providing low resistance. Cold-Welded, Gold-Plated Terminations This plug design allows for a connection devoid of solder, which is a common source of distortion.

Instead of solder, the process employs a high-pressure technique. Because the ground shells are stamped instead of machined, the metal used can be chosen for low distortion instead of machinability.

Sensitivity
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone sensitivity measures how loud a pair of headphones will be at a given signal strength. Headphones with higher sensitivity ratings will produce louder sounds than headphones with lower sensitivity ratings. It is measured in dB SPL (decibels of sound pressure level) per unit of power (typically 1 milliWatt) or sometimes unit of voltage (typically 1 Volt) from the source at a frequency of 1 kHz.

Frequency Response
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone frequency response refers to the frequency-specific sensitivity of the output. Frequency responses show the range that headphones are capable of reproducing—a graph shows which frequencies are accentuated over others. The ideal range covers the audible sound range of 20 Hz – 20 kHz.

Warranty

                      Warranty differs from manufacturer to manufacturer. Warranty covers factory defects but most manufacturers do not cover drops, water damage, driver damage, mistreatment of the product, etc.. It is always best to look at the manufacturer's website for the most up to date warranty information.

products.name: Zähl HM1 Reference Desktop Headphone Amplifier

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
3 of 17 remaining Only 50 Zahl HM1s are being made annually. com is the exclusive place in North America to buy the Zaehl HM1 Reference Desktop Mixing Headphone Amplifier.

Highlights Pure analogue design Consistent dual-mono layout Logic circuits without clock generators Straight linear power supply with power transformer in external housing No-compromise selection of components No-compromise interior and exterior construction Perfect impulse reproduction Ultra wide frequency response Extremely low impedance output precisely controls complex loads The Zähl (pronounced Zaehl) HM1 is high-quality fully analogue, Class A reference headphones mixing amplifier designed with no compromise to offer an unprecedented level of transparency and detail that will thrill the most discerning professionals and audiophiles alike. The Zähl HM1 also includes two different stereo source input with a cross-fade, Precise two band EQ and a stereo base control.

Its design is meant to offer the most true-to-life reproduction possible. Two Different Power Stage The Zähl HM1 features two operation modes Class A and Class A + Servo.

The first mode delivers the purest sound with no crossover distortion and no artifacts causing negative feedback. The second mode uses the same Class A circuit but adds negative feedback to correct errors that occur between the power amplifier and headphones.

While both modes offer technically superior performance, each mode will appeal to different users. Mixing Features The HM1 includes two input sources which can be used for critical A/B comparison of different DA converters, cartridges or comparing different mixes or effects.

Each input has a dedicated volume control for precise level matching. Each input can be hard switched or gently cross-faded.

The two sources can also be used to be mixed together. The new mix is fed to the headphones as well as the line outputs which can be used to connect to a recording system or active speakers.

Sound processing The HM1 includes a subtle two band EQ with fixed frequencies and gentle boost or cut. Unlike traditional tone controls found on amplifiers, it uses proven circuits used in studios to make subtle tonal accent changes rather than affecting the sound character.

The HM1 also includes a Stereo Base control akin to the circuit used in their IM1 module or AM1 console which lets you widen the stereo field without losing information in the Mid channels. This processor is useful to check the spatiality of a mix ranging from mono (fully left) to really wide.

The Stereo base stage can be completely switched out of the signal to maintain the signal as pure as possible. A Balance control also lets you compensate for any balance discrepancy whether in the mix, the headphones or the user’s hearing.

5dB on either side. Dual Mono Design The HM1 uses a dual mono design strictly separating left and right channels, avoiding any interference between channels.

Each channel has its own power supply for both the preamplifier and power amplifier stage. Furthermore, the Mains transformer includes independent and completely potential-separated windings for each channel while filtering, voltage regulation and rectification are individual to each channel.

5mm Jack output and an XLR 4-pin connector. Using the latter ensures the perfect maintenance of the dual mono principle with no interference occurring at any point.

The Power supply uses a purely linear design and includes a wide range input. Using one of the best interference filters available, the mains input can be set to operate at the following voltages: 100V, 110V, 120V, 220V, 230V, 240V.

Power Stage Class A - HM1 realisation The HM1 power stage provides massive power reserves, which is already evident from the fact that it consumes almost 40W in idle mode. The output power is more than sufficient for any application, and in the millisecond range it is increased substantially.

The output resistance is remarkably low. The optimum operating point of the power stage was first specified by theory, then by measurements on the sample units and finally fine-tuned during numerous listening tests with experts, especially mastering engineers.

The same applies to the selection of components. This meticulous way of design largely compensates for the possible disadvantages of Class A described in the theory paragraph below.

Class A & Servo - HM1 realisation To take Class A one step further, we implement an idea which is as simple as it is ingenious: We take the best of Class A and the best of negative feedback amplifiers and put it together: Class A operation is supplemented by negative feedback ("Servo"). Since there is no crossover distortion, there is nothing for the feedback circuitry to correct.

Rather, it only corrects the errors which result from the interaction between the power amplifier and the headphones. The feedback path is designed in such a way that no artefacts are created by the correction.

The output resistance drops to a value which is smaller than the sum of headphones cables and connectors. In this way, headphone systems can be controlled precisely.

One can say that with the HM1, any headphones sound as they should. Why Class A and Class A & Servo?

The previous paragraph may lead to the conclusion that the optimum is achieved with Class A & Servo operation. So why do we still have the switching option?

Quite simply because we judge our circuits by ear. Our Class A amplifier was developed with the highest musical demands in mind.

We experienced that is does not sound the same as the servo version, but it sounds equally outstanding. Depending on headphones, music and personal preference, the user can make his choice.

Even we were surprised to find that despite clearly different characteristics and measurement results, the hearing difference is rather subtle. Disadvantages: The internal resistance of the output transistors and usually also the emitter or collector resistors are in series with the load.

Simplified, one can say that the material properties of the output stage components substantially determine the sound. the headphones, are complex items, the result is also complex: it is quite common that certain combinations of even very high-quality amplifiers and headphones do not produce optimal results.

Experienced audiophiles know this experience. Class AB with negative feedback Advantage: Any error at the output caused by the effects described above is "corrected" by a negative feedback circuit.

And furthermore, the output resistance of the power amplifier, as long as there is no overload condition, theoretically approaches zero; practically it is in the 2-digit milli-ohm range. The complex internal resistance of a headphone system is almost equalised by the low impedance output.

A headphone system is therefore tightly “guided” by the power amplifier. Disadvantage: The crossover distortion occurs first, then it is corrected.

Thus, negative feedback control (at least theoretically) always runs a little behind the action, which can lead to artefacts in the signal. However, modern negative feedback audio power amplifiers are usually not purely Class AB.

Very effective techniques are used to keep crossover distortion low without having to use the costly and power-intensive Class A technique. Certain techniques are used in the negative feedback signal, so that the "lagging" of the correction almost no longer plays a role.

Mixing Stage A/B comparison CConcerning the reference quality of the HM1, the idea of using it for critical A/B comparisons is most obvious - be it for evaluating different sources like D/A converters or cartridge systems in the high-end range or comparing different mixes or sound processing options in the professional range. For this purpose, the HM1 has two inputs with independent level control and on/off buttons.

Exact level matching is essential for a critical A/B listening comparison. By the way, the on/off function can also be operated via a cable remote control, which facilitates a blind comparison.

Cross-fade The mixing stage can also be used to crossfade two sources. A very musical alternative to the otherwise usual "hard" switching.

Mixing two sources And of course this stage is suitable for mixing any two sources. A new programme is created from two music programmes.

This new programme can then not only be listened to in the headphones but is also available at the line outputs on the back of the unit, which can be used for connecting active speakers and recording units. This turns the HM1 into a 2-channel stereo mixing console with reference quality.

Also important: If only one channel is used, the mixing stage is not superfluous "ballast". An unused channel is switched off directly at the input stage and thus cannot negatively influence the signal integrity.

This switch-off is realised via relays and is triggered as soon as a volume control is set to minimum or a channel on/off button is in the off position Sound Adjustment This stage is not designed to massively affect the sound. As a rule, all audio gear connected to the HM1 is of extremely high quality, a classic tone control would not be appropriate.

However, it can be advantageous to make fine, precise adjustments in the frequency response domain, depending on the headphones, music programme or even personal preference. Low and high frequency adjustment The low and high frequency adjustment, each in three fixed steps as boost and cut, is primarily designed for musical purposes.

We have further developed proven circuits from studio technology to achieve a stage which sets subtle accents rather than changes the sound character. The basis are filters with selected components, of course all circuits are precisely switched by relays.

Professionals use the functionality, for example, to find out whether a mix is balanced in terms of low and high frequencies or can still be optimised. Stereo Base control, a little theory A special feature is the possibility to adjust the stereo width.

The perception of spatiality when listening with headphones differs from listening with loudspeakers. Instead of a cross-feed circuit, we use our stereo base width setting.

It is based on the mid/side technique which is commonly used in professional studios. It provides additional benefits.

The stereo signal is converted into a mid signal (in simple terms, what L and R have in common) and a side signal (in simple terms, what distinguishes L and R). Summing mid and side signals in a 1:1 ratio will result in the original stereo signal.

However, if you change the ratio between mid and side before summing them, you change the stereo base width. In our circuit, we leave the mid signal as it is.

We only adjust the level of the side signal. If we lower the level, the stereo image becomes narrower, if we raise the level, the stereo image becomes wider.

Stereo Base control, what it does You have direct access to the perception of spatiality. With a music programme which seems too "wide" in the headphones, one will turn the control one or two steps to the left.

If you perceive a recording as too "dry" (centred), turn the control one or two steps to the right. The leftmost position is mono.

This is the preferred setting for early stereo recordings, when individual instruments have been mixed to the extreme left or right - without spatial reference. Professional users check the spatiality of their mix with this function and may discover possible problems, especially in the extreme positions.

Also important: With the DIR (Direct) button, this stage can be completely switched out of the signal path. In this way, the purist approach is taken into account.

Balance A precision potentiometer with 21 detents is available for balance control. The centre position is perfectly calibrated and haptically clearly defined.

5 dB - caused by music programme, headphones or individual perception - can be compensated. Headphone Outputs + Balanced Connection XLR 4-pin connector and ¼ inch jack socket are wired in parallel and are intended for alternative use.

Theoretically, you could use both at the same time, the power amplifier is strong enough. However, for a reference quality listening experience, we do not recommend such use.

Ideally, the XLR 4-pin is used in conjunction with balanced wired headphones. In this case, the signal currents of the two power amplifiers are not mixed with each other, mutual interference is impossible.

The HM1 can unfold its full quality (also refer to chapter "Dual Mono Design"). Dual Mono vs.

Balanced amplifier design With its dual mono design, the HM1 features the same advantages as a balanced output stage but avoids the drawbacks. The drawbacks of a balanced output stage are the significantly increased number of electronic components - a balanced output contains two output stages per channel which work in reverse phase.

Two output stages result in doubling the output impedance. ¼ inch jack compatible Another advantage of the HM1 architecture is that unbalanced headphones with ¼ inch jack plugs can also be operated without any problems.

Line Inputs Balanced signals (XLR) or unbalanced signals (RCA) can be connected to Line Input A and Line Input B. XLR and RCA must not be used simultaneously on the same input.

The Bal/Unbal switches set the inputs independently to balanced (Bal) or unbalanced (Unbal) mode. Each input provides another switch which adds an extra 15dB gain.

This ensures that even signals with low levels can be processed without any problems. Line Outputs The signal at the line outputs corresponds to the signal in the headphones, except that it does not pass through the headphones amplifier, but through balanced or unbalanced line output stages and is routed to connectors on the rear.

Connect active speakers, power amps or other gear Balanced and unbalanced outputs may be used simultaneously to drive power amplifiers, active speakers, level meters or other components. If, for example, the HM1 is used for comparing two stereo sources, the result may be recorded using one of the outputs.

"A Thru" Output The "A Thru" signal is tapped from Input channel A, post input amplifier. The switchable 15dB gain stage at Input A affects the “Thru” signal.

The Thru output has an unbalanced output stage. Setup your own test bench / experimental bench A signal connected to Input A can thus be routed to another application without loss.

Application example: "A Thru" is routed to a sound processing device or effects unit, the output of this unit is fed to Line Input B. The ratio between original and processed signal can be set by the A/B volume controls.

Of course, this setup is also excellent for testing any device: Channel A supplies the original, channel B the signal coming from the unit to be tested. Dual Mono Design The idea The idea behind strictly separating left and right channels is to keep any interference away from the circuits.

A term like “crosstalk” does not get to the core of the matter. Music signals usually have left/right references, so that an extremely low crosstalk value - moreover, usually measured with sine waves - does not mean so much.

But with music highly energetic signal pulses occur, and then high currents are individually demanded by the output stages. It is extremely important that in these cases there is no coupling via a common power supply or via ground lines carrying signal current.

Only this way an amplifier can produce absolutely undistorted output signals. Realisation inside the HM1 In the HM1, the power supplies for left and right channels are separate, for preamplifiers and power amplifiers.

The mains transformer has independent, completely potential-separated windings for each channel. Rectification, filtering and voltage regulation for each channel are individual.

For logic circuitry and front-panel indicators, there is another winding and separate rectification, filtering and voltage regulation. The ground potentials of the two channels are connected to each other at one point only, but this is done purely as potential equalisation; it is impossible for signal currents to be mixed.

Optimal output connection If the XLR 4-pin output is used in combination with balanced wired headphones, the dual mono principle is implemented in full consequence. When using the jack output, the ground wires of both channels are connected in the jack socket and the jack plug of the headphones.

The use of headphones with jack plugs therefore is not that ideal. (also refer to chapter: Headphones Outputs / Balanced Connection) Power Supply Mains voltage and mains transformer are always potential sources of interference - consequently, we have outsourced them to the HMP1 mains adapter.

The mains adapter also contains a standby power supply unit which delivers a stabilised low voltage. This voltage is applied to the Power switch on the front panel of the HM1 and serves to switch on the actual mains transformer via a relay.

Worldwide operation The standby power supply has a wide-range input, is a purely linear design and complies with the common standby power regulations. The mains input is equipped with one of the best interference filters available and can be set for operation on the following voltages: 100V-110V-120V-220V-230V-240V.

The mains switch on the back of the HMP1 can be used to completely de-energise the unit. Variable cable length The connecting cable between the mains adapter and the main unit carries potential-separated low voltages only.

The length of the cable is variable over a wide range and can be defined by the user when ordering.

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Pocket sized DAC for laptops, phones, and tablets Moondrop DAWN PRO is a compact USB C DAC amp that lets computers, smartphones, and laptops step up to real HiFi playback. 1 kHz up to 32 bit 384 kHz and DSD up to DSD512, so lossless and high resolution streaming services are fully covered.

Connect it to a USB C device, plug in your headphones, and you have a clean, powerful front end in the space of a thumb drive. Dual Cirrus Logic CS43131 for clean output Inside DAWN PRO, Moondrop uses a pair of Cirrus Logic CS43131 DAC amp chips with a dedicated USB interface, dual crystal oscillators, and three independent power supply stages.

Each section of the circuit gets its own regulated power rail, which helps keep distortion low, noise down, and dynamics wide while still keeping power draw reasonable for portable use. Independent 100 step volume control DAWN PRO uses its own 100 level hardware volume control that sits after the DAC.

This keeps the gain structure clean and separates the dongle volume from the system volume on your phone or laptop. The result is smooth volume adjustment and more precise control at low listening levels compared to relying only on the host device.

4 mm balanced output doubles the available voltage swing and current delivery. 4 mm jack (around 120 mW into typical loads), DAWN PRO has enough power to handle many full size dynamic headphones as well as portable planar models.

Low noise, high dynamic range Background noise is kept to the microvolt level and the balanced output reaches a dynamic range of up to 132 dB. 00014 percent on AES17 measurements, which means the dongle stays well below the noise floor of most recordings and headphones.

In practice this translates to a quiet background, strong contrast between soft and loud sounds, and clear imaging. Aluminum housing with thermal vents The shell is made from CNC machined aluminum alloy with an anodized finish for durability.

Heat vents sit above the chips that run warmest, a design borrowed from desktop HiFi hardware. This helps DAWN PRO stay stable during long sessions and heavy loads while keeping the exterior comfortable to touch.

Everyday use and compatibility DAWN PRO connects over USB C and works with many Android phones, laptops, and desktop computers. A USB C to USB C cable is included along with a USB A adapter for use with older machines.

iOS devices will need a suitable USB adapter from Apple or a powered hub. 39 mm Input USB C (UAC) What is in the box Moondrop DAWN PRO USB DAC amp USB C to USB C short cable USB A to USB C adapter User documentation

Renowned for their Exquisite Digital Audio Players, Astell&Kern Unveils the First DAP with Personalized Sound Features personalized sound through hearing test 160-step EQ control via the Sound Master Wheel Triple AMP Class with real-time switching Class A current control with high / mid / low modes Proprietary Enhanced Signal Alignment technology to minimize group delay Bloom's Take The Astell&Kern PD20 reimagines what a digital audio player can be, putting control and customization at the center of the listening experience. ￼ Sonically, PD20 delivers a clean, detailed, and spacious presentation with strong imaging and a natural sense of musicality.

Rather than chasing pure flagship-level technicality, it focuses on flexibility and user experience, offering a highly adaptable, engaging sound that can be tailored to your preferences in real time. Read our full review .

Craft Your Sound Finding the sound that truly suits you is the first step toward the essence of music. PD20 is designed to guide you on that journey.

Astell&Kern's first step in this journey was to start from the very beginning. Rather than creating a successor to the PD10, they created an entirely new audio device that will redefine your musical experience.

Through Personal Sound, you can create a sound signature tailored to your hearing, then precisely refine it to your taste using the Sound Master Wheel. An intuitive control that allows even the amplifier driving mode to be changed with a single touch.

Now, music is not just something you listen to. It is something you shape.

Quad-DACs Designed with a singular focus on sound quality, PD20 adopts the ESS ES9027PRO DAC in a Quad-DAC configuration. Four DACs operate independently to minimize inter-channel interference and deliver precise signal separation.

As a result, even the finest nuances in sound are revealed with greater clarity, creating a natural, analog-like presentation through clean, distortion-free layering. TERRATON ALPHA To create the ultimate DAP unlike anything experienced before, A&K further evolved and applied TERATON ALPHA, their Ultimate Sound Solution, incorporating its advanced and innovative audio technologies.

Through effective power noise reduction, efficient power consumption with stable amplification, and a precisely engineered audio output interface, it delivers sound that remains faithful to the original source. Triple Amp Architecture PD20 features three distinct amplifier classes, allowing you to directly choose both sonic character and driving performance.

Switching between amplifier classes is achieved through a physical slide key rather than a software menu, enabling intuitive, immediate control based on your listening situation. Class A mode delivers rich, high-density sound with minimal signal distortion, expressing a smooth, analog-like texture.

Class AB mode offers excellent balance and efficiency, providing stable dynamics and articulate detail. Hybrid mode combines the refined texture of Class A with the efficiency and power of Class AB, creating a new level of sonic balance.

Sound Tuned to Your Hearing Developed in collaboration with global audio solution leader Audiodo, Personal Sound is used in a DAP for the first time, creating a personalized profile exclusively for you and redefining how you experience sound. By precisely analyzing your hearing characteristics and independently compensating for left and right ears, it dramatically enhances clarity and balance.

Regardless of genre, volume level, or the headphones or IEMs you use, you can enjoy a consistently optimized listening experience. Sound Master Wheel The Sound Master Wheel, a key design element of the PD20, is seamlessly integrated with the Audiodo equalizer.
