products.name: Astell&Kern A&Ultima SP4000 | Digital Audio Player

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
A&K's SP4000 Shatters the Limit Set by the SP3000, Harnessing Advanced Octa Circuitry to Deliver a Purer, More Powerful Sound Experience Digital Audio Player with Snapdragon 6125 Octa-core processor First Astell&Kern Device to Feature Advanced DAR Technology Supports High Driving Mode for delivering premium sound quality Ultra Low Noise LDO Regulator for top-tier noise suppression Minimizes group delay with proprietary ESA (Enhanced Signal Alignment) technology Bloom's Take Astell&Kern has always treated their flagship DAPs as a platform to redefine what’s possible in portable audio and with the SP4000, they’ve done it again. While it may not deliver the same leap forward that the SP3000 brought over the SP2000, the SP4000 feels like a culmination of every innovation that came before it, refined to its absolute limit.

The build quality is, as expected from A&K, sublime—equal parts futuristic and artisanal. Yes, it’s massive, yes, it’s heavy, and no, your pockets won’t thank you, but one listen and you’ll forget all that.

Under the hood, the Quad-DAC setup, improved DAR processing, and High Driving Mode push its sonic performance into rarified territory. With IEMs or even challenging over-ear headphones, it delivers a vivid, expansive soundstage and a hyper-detailed yet cohesive image that feels more like a live performance than a playback.

Functionally, the SP4000 also marks a shift in Astell&Kern’s traditionally closed ecosystem. With Google Play preinstalled and true multitasking finally on board, the SP4000 softens the company’s “walled garden” approach and opens up to modern app use without compromising its player-first experience.

In the A&K lineup, the SP4000 doesn’t just sit at the top, it transcends it. While the SP3000 brought the revolution, the SP4000 perfects it.

It’s not merely Astell&Kern’s best DAP yet, it’s the DAP to beat. Read our full review .

Remarkably Close to Perfection The A&ultima SP4000 is Astell&Kern’s newest flagship digital audio player, the result of three years of relentless research and innovation following the development of the SP3000. Built upon an advanced Octa audio circuit architecture, the SP4000 distills the purest essence of audio engineering, delivering a sound experience unlike anything before it—refined, powerful, and remarkably close to perfection.

Discover the SP4000 and experience sound on an entirely new level. Snapdragon Octa-Core CPU A&ultima SP4000 is equipped with a Snapdragon 6125 Octa-core processor.

With its faster system response and a redesigned generation user interface, you can spend less time waiting for the music to load and more time enjoying the incredible sound. Combining with the high-performance CPU with 8GB of DDR4 memory lets SP4000 deliver fast and fluid movement with improved multi-tasking through Android OS.

To maximize the efficiency of the circuit and reduce heat, the CPU, memory and wireless communication parts are configured as one module, with the digital circuit parts arranged in the same area creating a single system on a chip (SoC). Enhanced Signal Processing with Octa Audio Circuit In the SP3000, the digital-to-analog signal processing structure was separated in a 1:2 ratio.

With the SP4000, it has evolved into a 1:1 architecture. This new structure, where one AK4191 digital processor is paired with one AK4499EX DAC , allows digital signals to be delivered precisely to a single DAC without the need to distribute noise, enabling improved signal separation and processing.

Through continuous research and innovation in circuit technology, the SP4000 successfully implements a true Quad DAC—a feat previously considered impossible due to noise and other issues. As a result, the SP4000 achieves an impressive SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) of 131dB, on par with the independent dual audio circuit of its predecessor.

Advanced Engineering for Unmatched Clarity High Driving Mode The SP4000 features twice as many OPAMPs arranged in parallel compared to its predecessor, delivering richer and more detailed sound. High Driving Mode provides powerful and stable output—much like a four-wheel-drive vehicle confidently navigating rough terrain.

It’s designed to reproduce even the most delicate sonic details with precision. Enhanced Signal Alignment Technology The SP4000 features proprietary ESA (Enhanced Signal Alignment) technology, which significantly improves one of audio’s long-standing challenges, group delay.

ESA technology aligns frequency signals to arrive more uniformly, minimizing frequency distortion and dramatically enhancing sound clarity and purity. Top-Tier Noise Suppression The SP4000 features a newly implemented LDO (Low Dropout) Regulator in its power supply, which reduces noise by up to 97% compared to previous models.

LDO Regulators help stabilize battery voltage and effectively suppress noise, resulting in cleaner, purer sound. Precision Sound with Any Layer HDI PCB To minimize signal loss, the SP4000 incorporates top-tier Any Layer HDI (High-Density Interconnect) PCB technology.

Commonly used in smartphones and high-performance electronic devices, this advanced circuit board allows for the precise design of complex circuitry within a compact space. Additional Features and Enhancements Sound Design Through DAC Filters With the SP4000, you can enjoy the fun of creating your own sound style by directly selecting various DAC filters provided by the DAC manufacturer.

5th Generation UI The SP4000 features an upgraded UI that balances both functionality and emotional experience. A&K's First Full Android OS Integration Astell&Kern has overcome Android OS’s sampling limitation (SRC) through its proprietary customization technology, ADP (Astell&Kern Direct Path).

6-inch 2K Display Experience the SP4000 more conveniently and comfortably with a wide 6-inch, large-screen 2180x1080 2K display. AK File Drop With the new AK File Drop function in the SP4000, you can freely transfer files wirelessly through a PC, smartphone, or FTP program located on the same network Automatic 'ReplayGain' and Uniform Volume Adjust ReplayGain adjusts sound sources with different volumes to identical levels so you can enjoy your own playlists seamlessly.

Material Innovations The SP4000 uses 904L stainless steel material that has never been attempted before in a portable audio player.

Using this material has expanded its value from just a digital device to the realm of a luxury good. Exquisitely neutral acoustic voicing brings your music closer, makes it more alive and vivid, yet pure and natural. Within this delicate balance, the IE 600 nevertheless manages to incorporate powerful yet fast and accurate low-end response.

It’s all in a day’s work for Sennheiser’s TrueResponse transducer, the single 7 mm driver responsible for the extra-wide frequency range and ultra-low distortion of the IE 600. Balanced, neutral voicing To achieve a natural sound reminiscent of the neutrality provided by high-end studio monitors, our engineers carefully tuned the acoustic back volume inside the nozzle of the IE 600.

This voicing lends a presence and intimacy that brings listeners closer to the music, allowing them to discover new accents and details. However, arriving at this level of poise and naturalness was not without challenges.

When similar sounds occur in a track simultaneously, for instance, it can become difficult for the human ear to resolve all the nuances. The IE 600 integrates dual two chamber absorbers (D2CA) which capture and attenuate these masking frequencies, revealing even the finest textures of your music.

Stronger than steel, built to last Researchers have worked for many years to perfect amorphous metals for manufacturing. The wait was worth it — the zirconium alloy from Heraeus Amloy Technologies we chose for the IE 600 has triple the hardness and flexural strength of high-performance steel.

Shock-frozen during manufacturing, amorphous metals never have a chance to form a crystalline structure like conventional metals. The result is a lustrous, satiny surface that is extraordinary resistant against corrosion and scratches.

The IE 600 housing is fabricated using metal-powder-based 3D printing that can create any shape imaginable within tight tolerances. Chambers and channels form as part of this additive manufacturing process with no milling required.

However, cost does limit the potential applications of this new material. One of the only places you’ll find it — besides ultra-high-end products like the IE 600 — is in the drilling head of a NASA Mars Rover where extraordinary resilience in extreme conditions is required.

Automated manufacturing, handcrafted finish Production of the amorphous metal housing takes place in Germany and includes both automated and manual steps. A computer-controlled laser sinters a thin coat of metal powder, welding the molten alloy to the already hardened material beneath it.

Layer by layer, the part builds up to its ultimate shape. A technician then removes any artifacts of the manufacturing process by hand.

After thorough cleaning, steel shot blasting, polishing, and sophisticated surface treatment, the housing assumes its final, extremely durable aesthetic. Even daily use leaves practically no evidence in the form of scratches or wear.

A faithful companion on your sonic journey Each TrueResponse transducer is assembled by Sennheiser and built to last. One of the most advanced production lines of its type in the world, our manufacturing facility has a singular purpose — to exceed the expectations of audiophiles.

products.name: Aune Audio BX2 Magnum Portable Headphone Amplifier

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Aune BX2 Magnum is a portable headphone amplifier with two genuine Korg Nutube 6P1 vacuum tubes, a fully balanced four-channel Class A circuit, and up to 5 watts of output into 32 ohms, running entirely on its own seven-cell battery bank. Almost nothing else you can fit in a jacket pocket attempts this.

The BX2 Magnum is built for listeners who refuse to choose between a serious rig and a portable one. 4mm outputs with a choice of two completely different sonic characters.

Two Amplifiers in One Chassis A physical switch selects between tube mode and transistor mode, and the two signal paths are fully independent, joined only by latching relays that switch without coloring the signal. 0003% THD+N from the balanced output.

Tube mode routes the signal through the Nutubes for the warmth, body, and harmonic richness tubes are loved for, with distortion up to 1% because that character is the entire point. Two gain levels and two Class A current settings multiply those characters further.

Between mode, gain, and bias, the BX2 Magnum offers eight distinct operating combinations to match headphones and mood. Real Tubes, Properly Driven The Korg Nutube 6P1 is a true dual-triode vacuum tube, and in the BX2 Magnum both tubes sit genuinely in the amplification stage rather than glowing decoratively behind a window.

A dedicated 30V anode supply pushes them into their optimal linear range, the voltage headroom portable tube stages usually lack. Ahead of them, a twin JFET input stage adds its naturally smooth transfer characteristic, and the fully balanced four-channel layout keeps left and right isolated for precise imaging.

Seven Batteries, Each with a Job Power is the reason the BX2 Magnum sounds like desktop gear. Its 14,000mAh battery bank uses seven independent 2000mAh cells: six form a true plus and minus 12V analog supply feeding the amplifier directly, while the seventh runs the digital control circuits in complete isolation, keeping control noise out of the music.

Two four-segment indicators on the rear panel track both banks in real time. A full charge over USB-C takes about five hours and delivers up to 13 hours in transistor mode or more than 8 hours in tube mode, enough for a work day on the solid-state path or a long evening on the tubes.

A Desk Mode, Thanks to the BP1 A five-pin external power input lets the BX2 Magnum bypass its battery entirely and run on plus and minus 15V from Aune's BP1 external power supply, sold separately and built in the same stackable chassis. On the desk it runs at higher rails than the battery provides while the cells sit idle; on the move the battery takes over again.

One amplifier honestly covers both lives. Measured Like a Desktop Amp The numbers hold up against amplifiers that never leave a shelf: output noise of 3 microvolts or less, signal-to-noise ratio above 117dB, and a 31-step R2R digital volume control that keeps channels matched at low listening levels with no contact noise.

High gain delivers 5,180mW balanced into 32 ohms and 644mW into 300 ohms, so hard planars and high-impedance dynamics both stay on the menu. Check your own pair against the table below with our headphone power calculator.

How the BX2 Magnum Compares Its closest relative is Aune's desktop S17 Pro EVO, which shares the twin JFET input and Class A philosophy with more raw power and a wall socket. The BX2 Magnum is the version of that idea you can take with you, and it adds something the desktop amp does not have: real vacuum tubes and a second sonic personality.

In the portable amplifier category, that combination has essentially no direct rival at $799. 4mm cable USB-C to USB-C charging cable Velvet pouch 4 spare silicone feet Quick start guide and warning card

products.name: Aune Audio YUKI Portable DAC and Headphone Amplifier

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Aune Audio Yuki is a portable USB DAC and headphone amplifier built around a choice almost nothing else in the dongle category makes: a fully discrete balanced amplifier with 16 transistors, the kind of output stage normally reserved for desktop gear. Aune then puts the analog board on display through a glass window in the snow-white aluminum shell, so the engineering is also the design.

4mm balanced outputs. It is made for listeners who want their in-ear monitors to sound like they are plugged into a serious system, wherever the music actually happens.

A Desktop Amp Idea in a Pocket Device Most compact USB DACs combine conversion and amplification into a single highly integrated chip, because space and USB power leave little room for anything else. Aune splits the Yuki into two stacked boards instead: one layer for USB input and digital-to-analog conversion, one dedicated entirely to the analog amplifier.

The amp layer carries 16 discrete transistors arranged as four independent amplification paths. A dual-boost converter generates positive and negative 5V rails for that amplifier, giving it more voltage headroom than a circuit running straight off standard USB power.

The analog board is built on a hybrid ceramic PCB, chosen for its thermal conductivity, insulation, and low dielectric loss, which helps the circuit stay consistent and preserves fine high-frequency detail. Two DAC Chips, One Per Channel Yuki uses two Cirrus Logic CS43198 DAC chips with one dedicated to each channel, so left and right are converted on completely independent paths.

Keeping the channels separate improves stereo separation and dynamics, which is exactly what preserves the sense of instruments occupying distinct places in a recording. Playback support covers PCM up to 32-bit/768kHz and DSD256, with Hi-Res Audio certification.

Lossless streaming from a phone, a high-resolution library on a laptop, and DSD files all stay within what the hardware can decode natively. Quiet Enough for the Most Sensitive IEMs Sensitive in-ear monitors reveal amplifier noise as a constant background hiss, so a portable DAC lives or dies by its noise floor.

00033% at 1kHz, quiet enough that reverb tails, room sound, and positional cues sit against silence instead of static. 5mm jack covers standard cables without an adapter.

Two hardware buttons handle volume directly on the unit, no companion app required. Phone, Laptop, and Nintendo Switch Connected to a phone or tablet, Yuki takes over from the device's internal audio with its dual-DAC conversion and discrete amplification.

Beside a laptop it works as a compact desk source for after-hours listening. 0 support means it also works with Nintendo Switch, where the low noise floor and channel separation keep game audio detailed and precisely placed.

Yuki is honest about its scope. It is built to make IEMs and efficient headphones sound their best, not to replace a desktop amplifier for power-hungry planars, and within that scope it applies engineering most of the dongle category skips.

Our portable DAC and amp collection covers the step-up options when you need more output. How Yuki Compares Dongles at this level usually reach for integrated solutions, like the current-mode amplifier modules in the Questyle M15i.

Yuki's discrete transistor stage is the outlier approach, and it is the reason the device sounds and looks the way it does: an analog-first presentation from a board you can literally see through the window. Our Dongle Wars Buying Guide maps out how the category's main contenders differ.

At $169, Yuki sits in the heart of the serious-dongle bracket and makes its case on architecture and tuning rather than raw output. Aune voices its products against real instrument recordings, and the goal here is the same as in its desktop line: natural timbre and musicality first.

products.name: Aune Audio N7 Headphone Amplifier

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
5 watts of balanced output into a chassis just over eight inches wide. It borrows the architecture of much larger amplifiers, twin JFET input stage, R2R volume control, and selectable Class A bias current, and makes that recipe fit a desk where space actually matters.

The N7 is a pure analog amplifier and preamp with no DAC inside: feed it from any DAC or streamer over RCA or balanced XLR and it takes care of everything after the conversion. For listeners stepping up from a dongle or all-in-one to their first serious amplifier, this is the point where Class A stops being exotic and starts being affordable.

Real Class A, Warm on Purpose Class A means the output transistors conduct continuously instead of switching on and off with the signal, which eliminates crossover distortion and keeps the amplifier in its most linear range at all times. The sound this design is known for is smooth, full-bodied, and naturally warm, and the N7 runs true Class A rather than borrowing the label.

The input stage uses matched twin JFETs packaged together so both devices heat and behave identically, keeping the circuit's midpoint voltage stable and the character consistent. JFETs are the reason the N7 earns its tube-like description: high input impedance and a naturally smooth transfer characteristic, with none of a tube's fragility or maintenance.

Two Current Levels, Two Gain Levels, One Quiet Background Like Aune's flagship amplifiers, the N7 offers dual-level Class A bias current: A-L for everyday listening and A-H for a fuller, more forceful presentation, shown in blue or red on the display along with real-time temperature. Two gain settings then match the output to the headphone, from sensitive in-ear monitors on low gain to demanding full-size headphones on high.

0004% at 1kHz. In practice, IEMs get silence instead of hiss, and hard-to-drive headphones get 6,570mW into 32 ohms or 750mW into 300 ohms from the balanced output.

A full aluminum chassis with side heatsink fins keeps sustained Class A operation stable. R2R Volume That Stays Balanced at Night The N7 uses two JRC R2R electronic volume chips with dedicated op-amps, forming a four-channel balanced volume chain.

Unlike a conventional potentiometer, which loses left-right balance at the bottom of its range, this control stays matched at the low levels where late-night listening actually happens, and it preserves imaging and stage while doing it. One multifunctional knob handles volume, gain, current level, and headphone or preamp switching, with a 3-inch display keeping the current state readable from across the desk.

An aluminum remote is included, so the N7 works as well from a couch as it does at arm's reach. 4mm balanced), two line inputs (RCA and XLR), and two preamp outputs (RCA and XLR), with an independent Class A preamp function.

Plug in powered monitors or a power amplifier and it becomes the control center of a compact desktop system, headphones by night, speakers by day. Power comes from an external 18V adapter, which keeps AC conversion outside the chassis.

Component selection follows Aune's desktop line: Panasonic electrolytic capacitors, WIMA decoupling capacitors, and a communication-grade PCB. How the N7 Compares The natural reference point is Aune's own S17 Pro EVO, which shares the same design ideas: twin JFET input, R2R volume, selectable Class A current.

products.name: Aune AR9000 Headphones

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Aune AR9000 is Aune's flagship open-back headphone, built around a 50mm dynamic driver that pairs a stacked carbon fiber diaphragm with up to 4mm of linear travel. That long, controlled stroke is the point of the whole design.

Bass arrives with real physical presence, big dynamic swings stay composed, and music opens up the way it does from a good pair of loudspeakers. The AR9000 sits at the top of Aune's Air Reference Series, the line that made Aune a serious name in open-back headphones.

It is built for listeners who want speaker-scale sound at a desk or in a listening chair: put on jazz, orchestral, or electronic music and it answers with weight, air, and space. Dynamics You Can Feel Most headphones shrink the distance between a drum hit and the quiet around it.

The AR9000 keeps that contrast intact. Kick drums land with a small pulse of moving air, bass lines reach into the lowest octave without smearing, and crescendos grow instead of simply getting louder.

Aune rates the frequency range at 4Hz to 50,000Hz, and the low end is the first thing most listeners notice. Tonally, the AR9000 stays balanced rather than boosted.

In our first impressions, our review team called it one of the most normal sounding headphones they heard at its debut, and meant it as high praise: vocals sit exactly where they should, and the crucial 1kHz to 2kHz midrange region is filled in rather than scooped out. A Driver Built Like a Miniature Loudspeaker The punch comes from engineering borrowed from high-end speaker design.

Aune's Omni-Stack Carbon Diaphragm layers continuous carbon fibers at precise angles with no cross-weave, so the driver is extremely stiff for its weight and resists the flexing that blurs fine detail. Zone-specific heat treatment then tunes damping across different areas of the diaphragm's surface.

Aune's patented Constant-Flux magnetic circuit keeps drive force consistent through the full 4mm stroke, while a new high-damping suspension with radial stiffeners holds that motion piston-straight. Behind the driver, a patented absorption and diffusion structure routes reflected energy through precisely shaped open and closed cavities instead of letting it wash back through the music.

03% at 1kHz, fast clean transients, and separation that holds together when a mix gets dense. An Open Stage, Angled Like Speakers Open-back means the earcups are acoustically open to the room, which trades isolation for a natural sense of space.

The AR9000 leans into this with Aune's Tilted Acoustic Matrix: each driver is angled so sound arrives at your ear the way it would from a speaker placed in front of you, not fired straight into the ear canal. Highly breathable mesh in both the front and rear chambers lets air and acoustic energy move freely through the housing.

The result is a wide, naturally layered stage with precise image placement and none of the pressure buildup that makes long sessions tiring. Like every open-back headphone, the AR9000 does not block outside noise and does not keep your music private, so it belongs in a quiet room rather than on a commute.

Built for Long Sessions At roughly 430g, the AR9000 is a substantial headphone, and the fit is designed around that fact. A wide suspension headband spreads the weight across the top of the head instead of concentrating it at one point, and the breathable earpads keep air moving around your ears so heat never becomes the reason a session ends.

The headband assembly is all metal, and the floating frame carries the precision-machined lines of the Air Reference Series. A deep metallic finish and honeycomb acoustic grille give the AR9000 a restrained look that matches how it sounds: controlled, confident, and built to be kept for years.

Easy to Drive, Every Plug Included With a 43 ohm impedance and 102dB sensitivity, the AR9000 is easy to drive by flagship standards. It reaches satisfying volume from modest sources, and a good desktop DAC and amplifier give its dynamics room to stretch.

4mm and XLR balanced connections. One cable moves between a laptop, a desktop rig, and a balanced amplifier.

An AuNest headphone case is included for storage and travel between rooms. How the AR9000 Compares The natural rival is the Sennheiser HD 800 S, the longtime reference among open-back dynamic headphones.

Our first listen left us calling the AR9000 the punchier alternative: its midrange is more filled in, its bass carries more weight, and it trades some of the HD 800 S's diffuse, panoramic staging for a more focused, closer presentation. At 43 ohms it is also far easier to drive than the 300 ohm Sennheiser.

Within Aune's own lineup, the AR9000 stands above the AR5000 MK2, the headphone that earned Aune its open-back reputation on tonal balance alone. The AR9000 keeps that balance and adds the long-excursion driver, suspension, and acoustic control of a true flagship.

At $1,399 it is priced against established flagships, and it is engineered to argue with them. 4mm, XLR AuNest headphone case Quick start guide

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Aune AR5000MK2 builds on the foundation of the original AR5000 with a more refined acoustic structure, improved driver behavior, and a stronger physical design. It is a full-size open-back dynamic headphone made for listeners who want a natural, spacious presentation without giving up body, bass weight, or everyday drivability.

With its 50mm MLD dynamic driver, large-tilt-angle acoustic structure, low 28-ohm impedance, and upgraded all-metal headband assembly, the AR5000MK2 is designed to be both serious and practical. It can scale with desktop DAC/amp systems, but it is also efficient enough to pair with quality portable sources.

Refined MLD Dynamic Driver The AR5000MK2 uses a 50mm open-back dynamic driver with Aune’s Multi-Layer Distributed diaphragm structure. The MLD diaphragm is designed to balance rigidity and damping, helping reduce breakup that can occur in larger dynamic drivers.

For the MK2 version, Aune further optimized the diaphragm material and surface treatment. The result is clearer treble extension, a more open sense of air, and improved smoothness through the upper frequencies.

Full-Range Balance with Greater Extension Aune tuned the AR5000MK2 for a natural, complete tonal balance. Compared with the previous generation, the MK2 extends both the sub-bass and ultra-high frequencies while refining the transition from the mids into the highs.

The low end is designed to have more authority and body without losing speed or articulation. Vocals and instruments remain coherent across the spectrum, giving the AR5000MK2 a sound that is spacious, balanced, and easy to settle into for long listening sessions.

Large-Tilt-Angle Acoustic Structure The AR5000MK2 uses Aune’s large-tilt-angle driver panel together with angled earpads to create a more expansive acoustic presentation. This structure is intended to improve the sense of depth, width, and vertical space while supporting more precise imaging.

The open grille housing and side venting help manage airflow and acoustic diffusion behind the driver. For listeners choosing an open-back headphone for music, gaming, movies, or critical listening, the AR5000MK2 is built around a more natural sense of space rather than a closed-in presentation.

Comfortable Full-Size Fit At approximately 365g, the AR5000MK2 remains light enough for extended listening while still using a more robust headband assembly. The headband shape and curvature have been optimized to improve fit across different head shapes, while the full-size earpads are designed to cover the ear without excessive pressure.

The breathable acoustic memory foam earpads help maintain comfort over longer sessions, making the AR5000MK2 a practical choice for desktop listening, focused work, late-night sessions, and long-form listening. All-Metal Headband Assembly The MK2 version upgrades the headband assembly to an all-metal construction for improved rigidity and long-term durability.

The design keeps the elegant visual language of the original AR5000, with a refined champagne-gold finish and clean industrial lines. The result is a headphone that feels more substantial without moving away from the comfort-first approach that helped define the original model.

Easy to Drive, Ready to Scale With a nominal impedance of 28 ohms and sensitivity rated at 112dB SPL at 1kHz/1Vrms, the AR5000MK2 is easier to drive than many full-size open-back headphones. It can work well with capable portable audio devices, while still benefiting from higher quality desktop DAC and amplifier pairings.

4mm balanced connections, making it easier to move between portable players, headphone amps, interfaces, and desktop systems without needing a separate cable immediately. 35mm interchangeable plugs Quick start guide

Impedance
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Usually between 8-600 ohm. Most consumer headphones have 32 ohm impedance. High impedance requires more power to run and requires external amplifiers to amplify the power to the required levels.

Sensitivity
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone sensitivity measures how loud a pair of headphones will be at a given signal strength. Headphones with higher sensitivity ratings will produce louder sounds than headphones with lower sensitivity ratings. It is measured in dB SPL (decibels of sound pressure level) per unit of power (typically 1 milliWatt) or sometimes unit of voltage (typically 1 Volt) from the source at a frequency of 1 kHz.

Frequency Response
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone frequency response refers to the frequency-specific sensitivity of the output. Frequency responses show the range that headphones are capable of reproducing—a graph shows which frequencies are accentuated over others. The ideal range covers the audible sound range of 20 Hz – 20 kHz.

                    More information
                    
                      Headphone sensitivity measures how loud a pair of headphones will be at a given signal strength. Headphones with higher sensitivity ratings will produce louder sounds than headphones with lower sensitivity ratings. It is measured in dB SPL (decibels of sound pressure level) per unit of power (typically 1 milliWatt) or sometimes unit of voltage (typically 1 Volt) from the source at a frequency of 1 kHz.

Frequency Response
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone frequency response refers to the frequency-specific sensitivity of the output. Frequency responses show the range that headphones are capable of reproducing—a graph shows which frequencies are accentuated over others. The ideal range covers the audible sound range of 20 Hz – 20 kHz.

    Impedance is a measure of the electrical resistance that a headphone's driver presents to the circuit powering it. Headphones with an impedance of over 120Ω (Ohm) typically require a dedicated amplifier.

Sensitivity
                        
                          
                          
                            



    

    More information

    Sensitivity is a measure of how much volume a headphone will produce for a given unit of power. The more sensitive a headphone, the less amplification it needs.

THD
                        
                          
                          
                            



    

    More information

    Total harmonic distortion describes how much distortion a headphone will produce at a given volume. The lower this number, the less distortion is produced.

Frequency response
                        
                          
                          
                            



    

    More information

    Frequency response is the range of frequencies that a headphone can produce at an audible volume. Ideally, a headphone's frequency response should cover the full range of human hearing (20Hz to 20KHz).

Speaker driver
                        
                          
                          
                            



    

    More information

    Speakers and headphones use a device called a 'driver' to create sound. Different types of drivers have different strengths and weaknesses, but can all produce great sound. Common varieties include dynamic, planar magnetic, and electrostatic.

The Meze Audio 109 PRO is a dynamic driver headphone with an open-back, over-ear design from Antonio Meze and his team from Meze Audio. Coming in at $799, the Meze 109 PRO is easily one of the best looking and most comfortable pairs of headphones you'll find in this price range.

Meze Audio 109 PRO - the most anticipated release of 2022 - is finally here The Meze Audio 109 PRO is Meze Audio's first dynamic open-back headphone, demonstrating Meze Audio's commitment to go beyond faithful reproduction of sound and convey pure emotion.

In a world of fast-moving technology, Meze relies on proven foundations. The new 50mm dynamic driver, assembled and tuned with the utmost precision, allowed Meze to push the boundaries of speed, accuracy and dynamic range.

Meze Audio's search led to the development of the 109 Series dual cone diaphragm - a combination of beryllium-coated polymer, cellulose and carbon fibre composite and a copper-zinc alloy.

Acoustic design at its finest - the spider-like structure and acoustically transparent grille inside the ear cup exposes the driver from both sides, creating Meze's most open soundscape yet. The velour pads comfortably enclose the ears and ensure an optimal seal to produce a natural sound.

Since velour is much softer and more breathable than leather, it also prevents sweat build-up and overheating during extended listening sessions. The 109 PRO is all about comfort - from the headphone's structural design to the choice of materials, all decisions have been carefully made to ensure the final product meets our highest standards of ergonomics.

With this in mind, Meze Audio have combined walnut wood, zinc, manganese steel and vegan leather into a comfortable, lightweight yet extremely strong structure. Meticulously tuned by Meze's in-house engineering team, the 109 PRO offers an emotionally engaging sound with great detail, clarity and just the right amount of punch.

Its organic character, coupled with superior dynamics, excellent imaging and full-bodied voices, brings soul-stirring details to life. Plus, it's easy to control from most devices, whether they're portable sources or complex home systems.

overviewFields.title: Description

The Genesis of Woo Audio's Smallest Innovation The quest to create a compact amplifier without sacrificing sound quality led Woo Audio to develop the TUBE mini. Inspired by their previous creations, WA8 Eclipse and WA11 Topaz, the TUBE mini is born out of the desire to integrate vacuum tube warmth into a portable solid-state amp.

This vision has culminated in a device that blends the best of both worlds. Introducing the TUBE Mini Woo Audio proudly introduces the TUBE mini, an ultra-portable vacuum-tube headphone amplifier and DAC.

It's designed to deliver impressively powerful sound in a device no larger than half the size of an average smartphone. The TUBE mini is the perfect companion for audiophiles who demand high-quality sound on the go.

Cutting-Edge Technology for Supreme Sound Quality The TUBE mini features traditional vacuum tubes combined with Woo Audio's innovative Mighty-Drive technology. This fusion offers the warm sound of vacuum tubes and the robust power of MOSFET amplification.

It includes a power management system, a tube headphone amplifier, and a high-resolution lossless DAC, all encompassed in a remarkably compact design. Vacuum Tubes on Full Display At the core of the TUBE mini are vacuum tubes, each amplifying a single channel, paired with the MOSFET Mighty-Drive technology.

This unique combination results in a sound experience unmatched by any solid-state or small tube amps, showcasing the robustness and longevity of tube technology. Minimizing Mechanical Vibrations Understanding the nuances of tube microphonics, Woo Audio has ingeniously mounted the tubes on a spring-loaded suspension system.

This design, akin to seismic damper systems used in earthquake protection, significantly reduces mechanical vibrations, ensuring a pristine audio experience. Signature Sound with ESS SABRE DAC The TUBE mini incorporates an internal ESS SABRE DAC, optimized for streaming and lossless playback of Hi-Res formats.

It delivers Woo Audio's signature sound, faithfully reproducing music with the authenticity and richness as originally recorded. User-Friendly Design and Highlights The TUBE mini is designed for simplicity and ease of use.

It features balanced and unbalanced outputs, supports high-resolution audio formats, and is USB bus-powered for plug-and-play compatibility with various devices. Its compact dimensions and lightweight design make it the ideal choice for audiophiles on the move.

Engineered for Audiophiles The TUBE mini is recommended for full-size, power-demanding headphones, offering a balanced headphone amplifier and DAC. Its specifications include a maximum power output of 1W @ 8 Ohms, a broad frequency response, and a high signal-to-noise ratio.

Crafted with an anodized aluminum chassis and available in multiple colors, it's not only a powerhouse of performance but also a stylish accessory. Craftsmanship and Portability Proudly designed and assembled in New York, USA, the TUBE mini exemplifies craftsmanship and innovation.

With its compact dimensions and light weight, it sets a new standard for portable audio excellence, offering audiophiles the freedom to enjoy high-fidelity sound wherever they go. The Woo Audio TUBE mini is more than just a portable DAC and tube amp; it's a testament to the harmonious blend of traditional audio technology and modern engineering, designed to elevate your listening experience to new heights.

specifications.title:
Sensitivity
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone sensitivity measures how loud a pair of headphones will be at a given signal strength. Headphones with higher sensitivity ratings will produce louder sounds than headphones with lower sensitivity ratings. It is measured in dB SPL (decibels of sound pressure level) per unit of power (typically 1 milliWatt) or sometimes unit of voltage (typically 1 Volt) from the source at a frequency of 1 kHz.

Total Harmonic Distortion (THD)
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      When driving headphones at high volumes, it is possible for the diaphragm (the ‘speaker’ inside the headphones) to be unable to move fast enough. This leads to distortion, manifesting itself as crackling, popping or the alteration of musical notes. Most headphones will fall below 1% THD.

Frequency Response
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Headphone frequency response refers to the frequency-specific sensitivity of the output. Frequency responses show the range that headphones are capable of reproducing—a graph shows which frequencies are accentuated over others. The ideal range covers the audible sound range of 20 Hz – 20 kHz.

Warranty
                
                  
                    
                      
                      
                    
                    More information
                    
                      Warranty differs from manufacturer to manufacturer. Warranty covers factory defects but most manufacturers do not cover drops, water damage, driver damage, mistreatment of the product, etc.. It is always best to look at the manufacturer's website for the most up to date warranty information.

Sound Signature Strada delivers a balanced and controlled presentation with a touch of warmth that enhances musical engagement without masking detail.

Bass is tight and well-defined with a subtle lift that adds weight and punch. The midrange stays neutral and transparent, preserving natural timbre and separation across vocals and instruments.

The ear pads combine a soft PU leather contact surface with an Alcantara-lined inner chamber to manage heat and moisture buildup. This design supports long listening sessions without fatigue and makes Strada easy to live with throughout the day.

Dynamic Driver Engineering At the core of Strada is a 50mm dynamic driver first introduced in the 109 PRO and carefully retuned for closed-back performance. The driver retains its natural character while being refined to perform optimally in a sealed chamber.

products.name: Aune Audio A17 Headphone Amplifier

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Aune A17 is the flagship of Aune's amplifier line: a fully discrete, fully balanced Class A headphone amplifier that delivers up to 11,500mW into 32 ohms. Aune's own tagline for it is two words, "drives anything," and the engineering underneath is what makes that a statement of fact rather than marketing.

The A17 is built for the listener whose headphone collection has outgrown polite amplification: inefficient planar magnetics, 600 ohm dynamics, and everything between. It is a pure analog design with no DAC inside, taking RCA or balanced XLR from your source and anchoring both a headphone system and, through its preamp outputs, the speakers next to it.

Class A Power That Holds Nothing Back The output stage runs three pairs of power transistors in parallel per channel, which lowers output impedance to 1 ohm, sharpens transient response, and keeps a firm grip on difficult loads. At maximum gain the balanced output delivers 11,500mW into 32 ohms and 1,260mW into 300 ohms, with usable power all the way to 640mW into 600 ohms.

Numbers like that put the hardest headphones in the store within reach: a HIFIMAN Susvara gets the current it starves for elsewhere, and a Sennheiser HD 800 S runs on a fraction of what is available. Check any headphone against these tables with our headphone power calculator.

A Power Supply Split Like a Loudspeaker Amplifier Class A amplification turns supply voltage into dynamic range, and into heat. The A17 resolves that tension with a split architecture: the pre-amplification stage runs on higher voltage rails at plus and minus 20V for headroom and stage width, while the output stage runs at plus and minus 15V to keep heat in check without giving up drive.

A 100 watt toroidal transformer powers the analog section exclusively, backed by a filter capacitor bank totaling nearly 80,000uF. The display and control system draw from a separate supply, with control signals isolated through digital isolator chips so nothing from the digital side leaks into the music.

0005%. Twin JFETs In, a MUSES Chip on the Volume The input stage uses Aune's twin JFET arrangement in dual-transistor parallel configuration.

JFETs share voltage-control behavior with vacuum tubes, which is where the A17 gets its natural, layered, warm character; running matched pairs keeps that character stable as the amplifier heats through a long session. Volume runs through the JRC MUSES72323, a high-end R2R volume chip with 99 steps, synchronizing all four balanced channels to keep left-right imbalance out of the picture even at whisper levels.

Headphone and preamp outputs keep independent volume logic, so switching between headphones and powered speakers never starts with a blast at the wrong level. 5dB combine with two Class A current modes, A-L and A-H, to match the amplifier's operating point to the load.

Sensitive in-ear monitors on G-1 sit on a background quieter than 7 microvolts; flagship over-ears on G-4 get the full output. The dual-color display shows current mode, gain, volume, and internal temperature at a glance, echoed by a second small display on the top panel.

Heat is managed the honest way, with mass and surface area: an ultra-thick pure aluminum chassis with a multi-tiered internal heatsink structure channels warmth away from the circuit and spreads it across the case. The A17 is built to run warm and stay stable through all-day Class A operation.

Every function gets its own physical button, and an aluminum remote mirrors the front panel from the listening chair. How the A17 Compares Within Aune's line, the step up from the S17 Pro EVO is substantial: eleven and a half watts balanced against seven and a half, a 100W toroidal against 50W, four times the filter capacitance, four gain settings against two, and the MUSES72323 running the volume.

The S17 Pro EVO remains the smart buy for most systems; the A17 exists for the headphones that ask more than most systems can give. At $2,399, the A17 competes with the established names in summit-level amplification and arrives with an argument they cannot all make: true Class A, fully discrete, with power reserves that end the question of what it can drive.

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
6 microvolts. Those two numbers are the story in miniature: enough power for the most demanding planar magnetic headphones made, and a background quiet enough for sensitive in-ear monitors.

The S17 Pro EVO is the amplifier half of a serious desktop system. There is no DAC inside, by design: connect any DAC or streamer through RCA or balanced XLR and it handles everything downstream, driving headphones from three front-panel outputs or acting as the preamp for powered speakers.

It replaces the S17 Pro at the top of Aune's amplifier line, keeping the same Class A circuit and adding the usability the original lacked. Class A, and Why It Runs Warm Class A means the output transistors conduct at full current all the time, whether music is playing or not.

Because the transistors never switch off, the design avoids crossover distortion entirely and stays in its most linear operating region at every volume. The sound this topology is known for is warm, smooth, and dense, with low-level detail that stays refined as the level climbs.

Constant current means constant heat, and the S17 Pro EVO manages it honestly. Two selectable current modes set the character: A-L runs 100mA per channel for everyday listening, while A-H doubles it to 200mA for maximum current reserve and the fullest presentation.

Heatsinks, a bottom heat plate, and the chassis itself form one integrated cooling structure vented through the rear panel, and if the internal temperature reaches 69C the amplifier steps itself back to A-L automatically. It is built to run warm; give it some breathing room and it will hold stable Class A operation all day.

Twin JFETs In, 16 Transistors Out Aune builds the input stage around matched twin JFET transistors. JFETs combine very high input impedance with a naturally smooth transfer characteristic, which is why their sound is so often compared to vacuum tubes.

Using two thermally matched devices keeps the circuit's midpoint voltage stable as the amplifier warms up, so the tube-like richness stays consistent from cold start to hour three. The output stage uses two parallel pairs of transistors per channel, 16 output transistors in total across the balanced circuit, fed by a 50 watt low-ripple toroidal transformer and a 19,200uF capacitor bank.

Power for the digital control circuitry is kept separate from the analog supply so the audio path stays free of interference. 00024% THD+N at 1kHz, vanishingly low distortion for a high-current Class A design.

Power for the Hardest Headphones on the Wall Inefficient planar magnetic headphones like the HIFIMAN Susvara are the reason amplifiers like this exist. The S17 Pro EVO delivers 7,500mW into 32 ohms and nearly 3 watts into 90 ohms from its balanced outputs, real current reserves for headphones that starve on smaller desktop amps.

High-impedance dynamics are covered too: 908mW into 300 ohms is far more than a Sennheiser HD 800 S will ever ask for. You can check your own headphones against these numbers with our headphone power calculator.

Two gain levels make that power usable across the whole range. 5 watts.

35mm single-ended outputs on the front panel. Volume You Can Trust at Whisper Levels Volume is handled by a four-way balanced R2R resistor network built around a JRC volume chip with dedicated op-amps.

Unlike a conventional potentiometer, which drifts out of balance at the bottom of its range, the R2R control keeps left and right channels matched at exactly the low levels where late-night listening happens, and it preserves staging and image placement while doing it. Day-to-day control is simple: one multifunction knob adjusts volume, gain, and current mode, and a 4-inch display shows input, gain, mode, volume, and internal temperature at a glance.

The interface shifts between blue for A-L and red for A-H so you always know how hard the amp is running, an automatic screen-off option keeps the desk dark, and the all-aluminum remote handles everything from the couch. A Preamp When the Headphones Come Off The S17 Pro EVO doubles as a proper analog preamp.

Headphone and preamp operation are selected independently, and each mode remembers its own volume setting, so switching from headphones to powered speakers does not start with a lunge for the knob. Balanced XLR and RCA preamp outputs feed active monitors or a power amplifier, and two line inputs let a balanced DAC and a second source stay connected at once.

In an all-Aune stack it is the natural partner for the AR9000 flagship open-back, with the balanced power and Class A control to show what that 50mm carbon fiber driver can do. It fits just as naturally under any DAC you already own.

What EVO Changes, and What It Keeps Compared with the original S17 Pro, the EVO adds the operational polish the platform deserved: independent switching between headphone and preamp output, separately stored volume for each mode, and the automatic screen-off function. 5 watt balanced output stage carry over intact.

At $799, the S17 Pro EVO makes a simple case: genuine high-current Class A sound, enough clean power for any headphone in the store, and preamp flexibility that lets one box anchor both your headphone and speaker listening. 6uV (high gain) Power Supply 50W low-ripple toroidal transformer, 19,200uF capacitor array Display 4-inch color display with auto screen-off Remote All-aluminum remote control included Headphone Output Power Load Single-Ended Output Balanced Output 32 ohms 2,050mW 7,500mW 90 ohms 765mW 2,970mW 300 ohms 235mW 908mW 600 ohms 117mW 459mW

These headphones are not just an audio device; they are a statement of uncompromising design and intent, created with the sole purpose of delivering music in its most perfect form.

The Solitaire P-SE stands as a testament to T+A's commitment to sonic perfection, with each component and sub-assembly crafted with unmatched precision and care. Exquisite Craftsmanship and Material Selection From the TPM 2500 converter system to the headband connections, every part of the Solitaire P-SE reflects the highest standards of craftsmanship.

Employing a variety of plastics, each chosen for their specific properties, the headphones offer a blend of internal damping, mechanical strength, and robustness. The surfaces are finished with top-quality lacquers, typically reserved for aviation applications, underlining the headphones' premium build quality.

The sophisticated design of the TPM 2500, coupled with the optimal arrangement of magnets and sound ducts, ensures linear sound reproduction, allowing music to flow naturally and authentically. A New Approach to Planar-Magnetic Headphones T+A has successfully circumvented the typical drawbacks of planar-magnetic headphones, such as low efficiency, heavy weight, and very low impedance.

This achievement stems from a novel approach to problem-solving, extensive design efforts, and the use of the finest materials available. The result is a headphone that fits together perfectly, with tolerances measured in the hundredths of a millimeter, ensuring a consistently flawless experience.

Comfort for Extended Listening Understanding the importance of comfort, the Solitaire P-SE's ear cushions and headband are handcrafted in Germany from allergen-free synthetic leather and velours. Optimal Open Construction The open design of the Solitaire P-SE sets it apart from closed systems, allowing the diaphragm to vibrate freely and unimpeded. This design choice ensures that the music signal is maintained in its purest form, free from any coloration or resonance issues that may occur in closed designs.

The RME ADI-2 DAC includes an improved SteadyClock, a fine-tuned to perfection analog circuitry, new MRC remote control, Extreme Power headphone output and a very special IEM output. With many fresh ideas, innovative features and numerous useful functions, the ADI-2 DAC quickly became the reference. Thanks to its combination of high-end DA conversion with two exceptional headphone IEM outputs and a remote control, it has received countless enthusiastic reviews for its sound, flexibility, and technical capabilities.

The current version of the ADI-2 DAC comes with an extended remote control, a further improved DA conversion and an adapted analog output stage for even better noise and distortion values. To address the home and HiFi users, RME exchanged some of the Pro's studio features with typical home and HiFi ones.

With an adapted feature set and much simplified operation RME proudly presents the ADI-2 DAC. Built on the technology, concept and features of the ADI-2 Pro, the DAC concentrates on DA conversion in top high-end quality, along with two exceptional headphone and IEM outputs.

The DAC Packed into the compact half 19” format factor, this little gem is filled with the finest high-end electronics, offering a reference class conversion from SPDIF coaxial, SPDIF optical (ADAT compatible) and USB to RCA, XLR, TRS and mini-TRS. As the most versatile DAC available, the ADI-2 DAC offers balanced/unbalanced analog I/Os, an Extreme Power headphone output, a super low noise IEM output, SteadyClock FS, 4-stage hardware output level control, DSP-based signal processing, external power supply operation, Class Compliant USB compatibility, sample rates up to 768 kHz as well as DSD and Direct DSD playback.

The SPDIF input signal can even be recorded via USB - as one would expect from RME the DAC is a true 2 channel Full Duplex audio interface. Improving DA The updated ADI-2 DAC uses ESS's ES9028Q2M in a special circuit variant developed by RME engineers that allows the chip to perform at its best.

With noise levels of 123 dBA, distortion less than -120 dB, or THD+N of -116 dB, the device delivers outstanding measured values. Even the IEM output, with -118 dBu already the world's lowest noise headphone output, improves to a sensational -121 dBu.

In addition, there is 4 dB of digital headroom, so that even high intersample peaks do not produce any audible distortion. 5 dB result in a still undistorted analog output signal.

All these improvements are completely transparent in the previous menu navigation. There are no changes in operation, features and behavior compared to the predecessor, which is why neither appearance nor name have changed.

The only difference: with 'Low Dispersion' another digital filter is available for selection. Explanations for this filter can be found in the detailed manual of the ADI-2 DAC.

Super Low Noise for IEM lovers The headphone revolution not only brought headphones but also IEMs (in ear monitors) back into the attention of audiophiles and music lovers. Modern IEMs have a reference sound that easily competes with bulky over-ear headphones, making them not only a mobile alternative, but also an interesting solution in home.

Modern IEMs are extremely sensitive and operate on very low voltages. As a side effect they uncover the noise floor of the player, DAC or headphone amp.

When RME developed its Extreme Power headphone stage the basic noise floor was taken care to be as low as possible. Which was then confirmed in many reviews (most black background…).

Even when used with IEMs. Still RME wanted to make sure that even the most sensitive IEM combined with the most sensitive listener receive the full dynamic range on playback.

Also capable outputs like the Extreme Power ones are not fully safe against operating errors and might blow up ears or IEMs. RME's solution: adding the most advanced IEM output imaginable as second phones connection to the front of the ADI-2 DAC.

Its ground noise floor is an astounding 10 dB lower than the one of the Extreme Power output (black hole background…), output impedance is near zero Ohms, THD reaches new record lows, click-free on/off is included as well as volume ramp-up, and the sound quality with any IEM is just amazing. We're sure you will love it!

Lights Out! A studio converter with all lights off?

Defective. But on a DAC it was one of the most often requested features from our ADI-2 Pro HiFi customers.

Here we go: display, function keys, volume knob, even the standby button - they all go off after 10 seconds of no user operation when AutoDark is activated in the unit's menu. Touching any button or control will turn on all lights for 10 seconds.

Using the remote AutoDark can also be switched off / on, and using any button on the remote turns lights on for 3 seconds. Once again: we're sure you will love it!

New extended Multi-Remote Support (MRC) The ADI-2 DAC comes with a remote that is not the usual cheap add-on. This nicely designed remote control has clearly labeled buttons, readable even in low light conditions without reading glasses, a nicely laid out button arrangement that is easy to remember, and perfect button ergonomics.

Plus: It won't interfere with your ATV or other devices. The ADI-2 DAC remote control provides buttons for standby on/off, volume, balance, bass and treble, input selection (optical, coaxial, USB), mute, on/off loudness, bass/treble and EQ.

In addition, there are four programmable buttons that provide access to 32 different functions and commands for maximum flexibility. There is no other converter or comparable device with such a sophisticated, easy to use and at the same time versatile remote control!

Note for owners of the previous remote: the new MRC is also available separately as an accessory. It can be used with all ADI-2 DACs, even older ones, if they are equipped with the latest firmware (at least version FPGA 27, DSP 33).

SteadyClock FS The ADI-2 DAC is the first device in RME's range with SteadyClock FS. There is not much to improve with SteadyClock, it has earned its accolades over years of flawless operation in numerous RME devices, guaranteeing that using the internal clock will produce exactly the same sound as when using an external one.

SteadyClock highly rejects jitter and handles all digital interface formats in an exemplary way. That's why SteadyClock's design and behavior didn't change in the DAC.

With SteadyClock FS the focus was put on reducing the self jitter of SteadyClock to new lows, by improving its second, analog PLL circuit, and referencing both Direct Digital Synthesis and PLL to a low phase noise quartz crystal. The self jitter measured through DA conversion now reaches levels that usually are only available in master quartz clock mode, while SteadyClock still always runs in PLL mode - no matter if internal or external clock, sound is exactly the same (again).

The low phase noise oscillator driving the updated circuit reaches jitter specs lower than a picosecond (ps), an area called FemtoSecond. Hence SteadyClock FS.

Bit Test A bit test is used to check the playback path for unwanted changes in the playback data. Playback software can cut bits, add dither, or change the level - without these changes becoming noticed easily.

A poorly programmed driver can manipulate bits, and a playback hardware could be both badly designed and defective (hanging bits, swapped bits). Even such features as proper channel assignment, left/right synchronicity and polarity can be tested by a well-made bit test.

With a bit test, such errors can be detected and - more importantly - excluded. Bit Test Audio files (download)

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Our Take: The Audeze LCD-X Creator's Edition (and Premium Package) are one of Audeze's most popular headphones, with good reason. Made with studio engineers in mind, the LCD-X targets a neutral sound with a touch of warmth resulting in a more laid-back listen than what you would get from something like the Focal Clear or Hifiman Arya.

However, the LCD-X does weigh 612 grams so comfort can be an issue for some. The Audeze LCD-X Creator's Edition contains 1 x Single-ended 1/4" cable as well as Audeze's Economy Travel carrying case.

If you're looking for the LCD-X with more premium packaging, check out the LCD-X Premium Package which has 1 x Single-Ended Cable, 1 x Balanced 4-Pin XLR Cable and 1 x Premium Pelican Travel carrying case. The Audeze LCD-X High-Performance Reference Planar Magnetic Headphones (Lambskin Leather) is designed for professional mixing, mastering, and reference level personal Hi-Fi listening when connected to a low powered external headphone amplifier or portable device.

The headphones are sensitive enough to be driven by portable music players such as iPods, iPhones, and other smartphones. Instead of utilizing traditional dynamic cone drivers, the headphones implement a neodymium magnetic planar transducer design to deliver a frequency response of 5 to 50,000 Hz with a THD of less than 1%, an impedance of 70 Ω, an efficiency of 95 dB per 1 mW, and a total output SPL of over 130 dB when driven by 15 watts.

Magnetic planar technology differs from traditional dynamic cone designs by suspending a thin lightweight diaphragm within a parallel magnetic plane comprised of an array of magnets. The diaphragm is much lighter when compared to a traditional dynamic cone and has a printed circuit spread across a thin-film substrate on the surface of the diaphragm as opposed to a cone attached to a voice coil.

When the audio signal from the amplifier reaches the circuit, it magnetizes the diaphragm within the field and produces sound. The benefits of a magnetic planar design include faster transient response due to the lighter diaphragm, a wide frequency with low distortion, better heat dissipation, fewer moving parts for greater durability without the kind of sonic degradation that cones are susceptible to, and better amplifier compatibility because the circuit functions as an almost entirely restive load.

The magnetic structure creates a uniform magnetic field across the diaphragm without the need for additional ferromagnetic material traditionally found in other planar headphones to remove magnetic interference, reduce harmonic distortion, and lower overall weight. The headphones also feature Audeze’s patent-pending Fazor elements that guide and manage the flow of sound through the earcups for a more enveloping sound stage and improved frequency extension.

The headphone earcups are made of anodized aluminum with black lambskin leatherette earpads. They come with a ruggedized travel case, a 1/4" to 4-pin mini-XLR cable.

products.name: Feliks Audio Echo Classic

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
The Feliks Audio Echo Classic is the most accessible way into the Feliks Audio tube amplifier lineup. Built as the purest expression of the Echo concept, it keeps the focus exactly where it should be: handcrafted Polish tube amplification, a warm and natural presentation, and strong synergy with high-impedance headphones.

As a simplified version of Feliks Audio’s best-selling Echo platform, Echo Classic is made for listeners who want the tube experience without paying for extras they may not need. It delivers the rich midrange texture, smooth treble, spacious imaging, and easy musicality people expect from a well-built OTL tube amplifier, all in a compact desktop design with classic wood side panels.

Pure Tube Sound, Made More Accessible Echo Classic is designed as a gateway into premium tube audio. It is not overloaded with features, switching options, or unnecessary complexity.

Instead, Feliks Audio has stripped the formula back to the essentials: a clean signal path, a proper OTL tube circuit, carefully chosen tubes, and enough power for the high-impedance headphones that pair best with this kind of amplifier. The result is a headphone amp that feels immediate and inviting.

Vocals have body, instruments carry natural texture, and treble stays smooth without losing air. It is the kind of sound that makes long listening sessions feel relaxed and immersive rather than clinical or fatiguing.

Built for High-Impedance Headphones Echo Classic is optimized for headphones from 80Ω to 600Ω, making it a natural match for many of the dynamic-driver headphones that tube amp fans love most. With 350mW of output power and 20dB of gain, it has the voltage swing and character needed to bring out the richness, scale, and tonal density that make high-impedance headphones so rewarding.

This is where OTL tube amplification makes the most sense. Pair Echo Classic with the right headphone and you get a presentation that feels open, full, and human, with a touch of warmth that flatters without smearing the music.

Classic OTL Character OTL stands for output transformerless, a tube amplifier design that removes the output transformer from the headphone signal path. For the listener, that design can translate into a more direct and expressive tube sound, especially with medium to high-impedance headphones.

Echo Classic uses a pair of driver tubes and a pair of power tubes to deliver the kind of sound Feliks Audio is known for: smooth, spacious, slightly warm, and naturally detailed. It gives music a sense of weight and flow without making the amp sound slow or overly soft.

Simplified Construction, Feliks Craftsmanship The Echo Classic is intentionally simple, but it does not feel basic. It is handcrafted in Poland with the same attention to fit, finish, and long-term reliability that defines Feliks Audio’s higher-end amplifiers.

The compact metal chassis and wood side panels give it a timeless desktop look that feels equally at home in a focused headphone system or a smaller office setup. By keeping the design streamlined, Feliks Audio makes the Echo Classic easier to place, easier to use, and easier to recommend as a first serious tube amplifier.

No clutter, no unnecessary extras, just the core tube experience done properly. 8 cm What’s in the Box Feliks Audio Echo Classic tube amplifier 1 pair of driver tubes 1 pair of power tubes AC cord User manual Warranty card

products.name: Astell&Kern A&ultima SP4000T | Vacuum Tube Digital Audio Player

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Discover the Astell&Kern SP4000T, the Ultimate DAP, Where Analog Warmth and Digital Precision Collide Copper Finish Coming in the Near Future Industry-first DAP with MIL-Spec Vintage Vacuum Tube Raytheon JAN6418 in Quad Configuration Industry-first DAP with Triple Tube Mode (Triode, Ultra Linear, Pentode) T Series Signature feature: Triple AMP System Adjustable Tube Current with Three Levels High Driving Mode, ESA, and Advanced DAR for superior sound quality Full Open Android Bloom's Take Astell&Kern has never been shy about experimenting at the top, and the SP4000T might be their most flexible flagship yet. Rather than chasing a single “perfect” tuning, it builds on the SP4000’s technical foundation and adds a tube stage that lets you reshape the sound to match your preferences.

It’s less about redefining performance outright, and more about expanding how you experience it. Sonically, the SP4000T still delivers the detail, imaging, and expansive staging you expect from a summit-fi DAP, but the real story is how it presents that performance.

In solid state, it leans clean and resolving, while the tube modes introduce varying degrees of warmth, body, and smoothness. Whether you prefer the lush, rounded character of Triode, the balance of Ultra-Linear, or the more energetic clarity of Pentode, each mode feels intentional rather than gimmicky, offering meaningful shifts in tone and texture.

Read our full review . A New Standard in Tube Configuration With independent dual-tube structures dedicated to the left and right channels respectively, the channel-separated design, once exclusive to home audio high-end tube amplifiers, has finally been brought to the world of DAPs.

The four tubes in the SP4000T work in a differential configuration, with each pair facing the other in mirror symmetry. In this precise balance, music signals are amplified with twice the clarity, while common-mode noise is mutually cancelled and eliminated.

When four hearts beat as one in perfect balance, the tube's signature rich harmonics resonate with the deepest, most resonant sound ever heard in the SP4000T. Triple Tube Mode The SP4000T is the industry's first DAP to feature Triple Tube Mode.

Combined with the T Series Signature Triple AMP Mode and the Tube Current level adjustment first found on the SP3000T, it offers up to 54 possible combinations tailored to any genre or preference, a true Analog Sound Palette. Triode Mode: The Purest Voice of the Tube This mode brings out the richest harmonic texture unique to vacuum tubes, letting the breath of a vocalist and the trembling of strings gently dissolve into a lush, lingering reverb.

Ultra Linear Mode: The Aesthetics of Balance A design that blends the tonal color of Triode with the output of Pentode. The sound fades softly at its edges, yet carries a firm, solid core.

Pentode Mode: The Most Powerful Voice of the Tube Maximizing tube amplifier output and dynamic range, this mode retains the tube's signature warmth while stripping away reverb — delivering a clean, powerful presence that speaks with directness and force. The Perfect Harmony A&ultima SP4000T, built on Astell&Kern's exclusive Teraton Alpha technology, achieves a perfect fusion of true analog sound from the Quad-configured Real Vacuum Tubes and the dynamic sound of the OPAMP.

SP4000T offers TUBE AMP mode for the authentic analog sound of a tube amplifier, OP AMP mode delivering Astell&Kern's signature clarity and expansive soundstage, and HYBRID AMP mode combining the best of both analog warmth and high-resolution output. Anti-Microphonic Noise Architecture The greatest technical challenge in applying vacuum tubes to a compact portable device is achieving low noise even at high resolution and high output.

SP4000T introduces an upgraded 5-stage 2nd Generation Architecture (up from the previous 4-stage design) to suppress microphonic noise (noise generated in vacuum tubes from even minor external vibrations). HEXA Audio Circuit Structure The SP4000T integrates dual AK4499EX DACs, AKM’s latest flagship, paired with dedicated AK4191EQ processors for each left and right channel, forming a fully discrete audio circuit architecture.

Unlike conventional DAPs that handle both digital and analog signals inside the DAC, the SP4000T's audio circuit uses a dedicated digital delta-sigma modulator (AK4191EQ) to reduce noise in the digital signal before passing it to a completely isolated Analog DAC (AK4499EX) for independent analog signal processing. Premium Leather Case The bundled leather case for the SP4000T was crafted using 'MINERVA' leather from 'BADALASSI CARLO', a renowned leather workshop located in the San Miniato district of Florence, Italy.

Vegetable tanning is an eco-friendly leather-making process, slow and time-intensive, that tans hides using only plant-derived tannin extracts. Badalassi Carlo leathers employ the Tuscan vacchetta technique, after removing the hair from the hide, bovine bone powder-derived tallow is added during the vegetable oil tanning process.

products.name: Astell&Kern PD10 | Digital Audio Player

overviewFields.title: Description
overviewFields.value:
Astell&Kern's PD10 Marks a Bold Leap Forward in Digital Audio Players, Redefining Innovation with Cutting-Edge Technology Features (4x) AKM AK4498EX DACs + (2x) separate AK4191EQ chips The world's first DAP incorporating the new AK4498EX chip Full separation of digital / analog processing Volume wheel replaced with buttons for the first time in an A&K DAP Includes new docking cradle for home use Bloom's Take The Astell&Kern PD10 is a bold reimagining of what a digital audio player can be, a portable unit that confidently steps into desktop territory, blending minimalist design with serious sonic flexibility. Powered by a dual-gain amplifier system and smart impedance sensing, the PD10 adapts effortlessly to a wide range of headphones, while offering a clean, resolving sound with a natural tonal balance.

Built around a quad-DAC architecture using four AKM AK4498EX chips and two AK4191EQs — with full digital-analog separation — the PD10 stands as the first DAP to implement AKM’s latest flagship DACs, delivering impressive technical transparency in a compact form. What sets the PD10 apart is its ability to shift roles, from on-the-go listening to full-fledged component in a high-end two-channel setup, thanks to the included cradle with XLR outputs and LED bit-rate feedback.

It’s not a DAP chasing flash or flair, but one that prioritizes control, usability, and seamless integration — offering an understated yet powerful alternative for listeners who want their gear to serve both lifestyle and audiophile needs. Read our full review here .

Venturing Beyond The PD10 is Astell&Kern's first product to venture beyond the constraints of their existing lineup. It represents a bold new direction in product design and innovation.

The PD10 embodies this evolution with a novel take on A&K's iconic volume wheel design. The DAP offers a more intuitive and distinctive path to optimal sound.

Complete HEXA Separation of Digital and Analog Astell&Kern equipped the PD10 with the same innovative HEXA audio circuit design first developed for the flagship SP3000. The PS10 consists of four AKM AK4498EX DACs and two separate AK4191EQ chips that handle digital signals.

Most digital players process digital and analog signals together inside the DAC. However, Astell&Kern’s advanced HEXA structure reduces the noise of the digital signal input through the AK4191EQ, a separate digital delta-sigma modulator, and the AK4498EX DAC is then designed to process the analog signals separately.

By physically and perfectly separating digital and analog signal processing, the PD10 delivers an astonishing level of sound that has seldom been experienced before. Independant Dual Audio Circuits To create not just a great DAP, but a truly innovative DAP, Astell&Kern worked to overcome the limitations of sound by designing an independent dual audio circuit for unbalanced and balanced outputs.

By creating two separate audio circuits, one for balanced output and a second for unbalanced output, Astell&Kern maximizes audio performance no matter what output is being used. Impedance Adaptive Dual Amps To cater to the diverse listening environments of users, the PD10 is equipped with two distinct amplifiers.

Different sound tunings have been applied to each amp, taking into consideration the average impedance of connected earphones and headphones. The Normal Gain AMP reproduces delicate details and delivers high-purity sound, faithfully reproducing the original sound.

The High Gain AMP excels in handling complex and dynamic sounds, rendering audio signals more vividly and with greater clarity for a more immersive listening experience. Additional Features and Enhancements Smart Gain When headphones or earphones are connected, the PD10 instantly detects impedance and auto-adjusts the AMP.

Its Smart Gain function ensures optimal amplifier matching, delivering a refined listening experience for all devices. Docking Cradle With its included cradle, the PD10 transitions from a portable player to a home audio source, offering USB charging, digital input, and XLR balanced outputs for seamless connection to speakers or a two-channel system.

Volume can be adjusted via the PD10 or set to a fixed line-out level, while an LED display indicates track bit-rate through color. Teraton Alpha, the Essence of A&K Audio TERATON ALPHA technology ensures playback that faithfully reproduces the original sound through noise removal, power management, amplification, and seamless audio output interface.

ReplayGain ReplayGain adjusts sound sources with different volumes to identical levels so you can enjoy your own playlists seamlessly. Native DSD512 The PD10 supports native playback of high-res PCM music up to 32-bit, 768kHz and DSD512.

AirPlay Support PD10 Supports AirPlay for iPhone users, allowing direct control while listening to music via AirPlay. Sound Design with DAC Filters Enjoy creating your own sound style by selecting up to 6 different DAC filters.
